authority: plan.json owns task content/graph; rendered Markdown is the human execution packet; conflicts block dispatch.

baseline.note: Archive manifest provenance is not a clean upstream commit or proof of validation.

sprints.title: Baseline, provenance, toolchain and evidence recovery
sprints.goal: Establish exactly what was supplied, what can be reproduced, which inputs are absent, and how parallel work will be accepted without inheriting historical green results.
sprints.risks: The fresh archive is not the exact earlier tested candidate; absent legacy sources, compilers, reviewers or platform executors remain explicit external constraints, never passes.

sprints.title: Final product contracts and explicit owner decisions
sprints.goal: Freeze one executable contract for the intended local production product, explicitly approve changes to prior policy, and make every implementation lane consume the same invariant set.
sprints.risks: Cycle-backed sprints, sealed submissions, review independence and scheduled status are recommendations until explicitly resolved; workers must not choose local alternatives.

sprints.title: Canonical persistence, revisions and migration foundations
sprints.goal: Provide immutable requirements, explicit identities and durable outcome/recovery records with schema constraints and safe upgrades; keep policy outside SQL storage mechanics.
sprints.risks: A new table or module alone is not a working product. Old empty profiles and conflated revision/fence fields require explicit migration dispositions.

sprints.title: One deterministic domain decision and action model
sprints.goal: Make status, reasons, timers, dependency truth and actor-specific actions deterministic over canonical facts, without conflating execution, integrity and service availability.
sprints.risks: The existing evaluator is a candidate, not acceptance. A correct pure decision cannot compensate for a store snapshot that omitted required facts.

sprints.title: Authenticated actors and project/workspace isolation
sprints.goal: Make directory/project/database selection and every actor/session authority check safe before lifecycle and public-surface expansion.
sprints.risks: Durable role lookup does not authenticate a caller. Lexical path checks do not guarantee resolved path confinement, and copying project metadata must not select a foreign database.

sprints.title: Versioned service, durable operations and snapshot plumbing
sprints.goal: Expose the canonical Rust decision and transaction model through one authenticated, bounded service contract with replay/readback and consistent notifications.
sprints.risks: Transport success is not mutation success. Unknown operations, cursor gaps and cached actor context must not let clients invent outcomes or policy.

sprints.title: Fenced multi-agent execution, leases and safe recovery
sprints.goal: Deliver one real ownership lifecycle with physical resource safety, exact deadlines, explicit recovery obligations and harness-neutral adoption.
sprints.risks: A database fence does not stop a process editing a shared worktree. Safe reassignment needs verified stop/resource disposition, not simply clearing current_attempt.

sprints.title: Profiles, genuine verification and immutable submissions
sprints.goal: Make required proof independent of observations, execute verifiers against real recorded inputs, and submit immutable attributable results without letting prose or fixture success close work.
sprints.risks: User-supplied hashes, shell command text or a receipt-shaped JSON object are not sufficient proof of actual execution against the required source.

sprints.title: Independent review, closeout, overrides and lifecycle reconciliation
sprints.goal: Complete every consequential acceptance, policy and recovery mutation transactionally, preserving raw truth and rejecting stale or unauthorized decisions.
sprints.risks: Accepted proof is not the same as closed work. An exception must not masquerade as a passed test, and reopening must not silently rewrite downstream accepted history.

sprints.title: Milestones, cycle-backed sprints and dependency planning
sprints.goal: Build the canonical planning model and familiar compatibility routes without duplicate sprint/cycle authority, preserving task identities through parallel scheduling and carry-over.
sprints.risks: Planning may start alongside runtime work, but cycle/container terminal-disposition integration explicitly waits for the accepted lifecycle gate where named on leaf tasks.

sprints.title: Exact projections, launch readiness and actionable queues
sprints.goal: Turn canonical work into fast, exact, explainable task/container/cycle views with server-owned actions, full totals and safe corruption handling.
sprints.risks: Bounded response pages do not imply bounded database work. Readiness cannot require all dependent tasks to be ready before a valid cycle can launch.

sprints.title: Versioned sources, curated memory and recoverable handoff
sprints.goal: Complete the launch source/memory workflow with trustworthy citations, project-local retrieval, Git publication recovery and useful revision-bound handoffs.
sprints.risks: Source content is untrusted data, indexes are derived, and Git publication cannot be one atomic transaction with SQLite. Memory must not become an alternate work authority.

sprints.title: Legacy parity, backup/restore and explicit maintenance recovery
sprints.goal: Migrate supported historical data without manufactured success, protect full project state with consistent backups, and expose explicit safe maintenance/repair workflows.
sprints.risks: The supplied v2 mapping is not the missing raw v1 evidence. Full retained parity cannot pass without representative originals or an explicit owner-approved scope change.

sprints.title: Complete human and machine CLI/service parity
sprints.goal: Make every accepted planning, execution, proof, review, recovery, knowledge and maintenance capability discoverable through thin supported public adapters.
sprints.risks: A registered command without full behavior is not parity; parser validation and human formatting cannot become a second policy engine.

sprints.title: Trusted workflows and no-goal multi-harness agent guidance
sprints.goal: Restore Boreal’s core self-guiding operating loop so an unfamiliar agent can plan, claim, prove, finish or recover using bounded trusted context rather than bespoke prompts.
sprints.risks: Workflow assets are guidance data, not authorization. Source text must not become shell argv or a competing persisted workflow state machine.

sprints.title: Production terminal workspace and recovery UX
sprints.goal: Deliver a premium, responsive service-client TUI with clear planning/execution/review/recovery surfaces, server-owned actions and safe behavior in short editor terminals and outages.
sprints.risks: Do not recreate lifecycle or action policy in TypeScript. Small terminals must reduce decoration before hiding data, selection, escape or consequential confirmation context.

sprints.title: Integrated real-service product conformance
sprints.goal: Demonstrate the complete cross-component product on one integrated source identity using genuine operations, proof and review—not feature-local or fixture-only success.
sprints.risks: A prior focused pass is input evidence, not acceptance of a changed combined tree. Owned corrupt-data setup is allowed only for negative tests, never to seed successful proof.

sprints.title: Adversarial security, fault tolerance, scale and soak
sprints.goal: Qualify the integrated product under hostile inputs, process/filesystem failures and sustained parallel workload, then repair and revalidate against preapproved budgets.
sprints.risks: Security and load tests must run against real supported boundaries. A skip, a lowered threshold or a unit-only pass cannot stand in for native fault/concurrency proof.

sprints.title: Reproducible packaging, installer and recoverable upgrades
sprints.goal: Build and install the full product as one versioned artifact set, verify actual runtime identity, and make updates atomic/recoverable without risking project databases.
sprints.risks: Source ZIP integrity and fake-release wizard fixtures are not production release proof. Existing update/upgrade routes must verify what was installed, not infer a version from output.

sprints.title: User onboarding, operator runbooks and support readiness
sprints.goal: Document the actual accepted product and give users/operators reproducible onboarding, recovery, maintenance and upgrade paths without internal implementation jargon.
sprints.risks: Documentation must be generated/verified against accepted commands and real transcripts, not aspirational routes or stale original plans.

sprints.title: Exact-artifact release qualification and independent cutover
sprints.goal: Qualify one clean final candidate on every supported platform and obtain an explicit evidence-based ship decision without publishing yet.
sprints.risks: A source change after qualification invalidates affected evidence. Test counts, old candidate logs and locally built packages are not an independent cutover decision.

sprints.title: Authorized publication, clean-install verification and operational handover
sprints.goal: Publish only the independently qualified immutable artifacts, prove that future users install those bytes, and hand over a recoverable production release.
sprints.risks: This sprint includes external side effects and requires explicit authority. A local candidate, uploaded source ZIP or generated tag plan is not a published production release.

tasks.title: Freeze the supplied snapshot and record evidence applicability
steps: Hash the fresh ZIP and verify safe member paths, CRC and every manifest member against bytes; preserve the input archive unchanged.
Record archive time, manifest source revision/dirty flag, tool-generated files and exact included/excluded paths without inventing an upstream commit.
Compare the fresh tree with the prior candidate/report and identify which retained logs refer to different bytes.
Create an evidence applicability table with source identity, command, environment, scope and historical/current classification.
Record any missing manifest or unreadable member as a finding; never rebuild the archive to hide a discrepancy.
Publish a source lock and immutable baseline identifier for all later task dispatches.
checks: The input archive hash before and after inspection is identical.
Every delivered-source file has a path, byte count and digest; unsafe or unmanifested files are explicitly accounted for.
Historical TUI/fixture passes and unrun Rust tests cannot be selected as current-tree acceptance evidence.

tasks.title: Establish a reproducible build and test environment
steps: Inventory Rust, rustfmt, Cargo, Node, npm, TypeScript, Python, Git, shell, tar and local-socket availability on each execution host.
Inspect committed lockfiles and build scripts before choosing install commands; record how the TUI compiler is provisioned rather than assuming npm ci is available.
Record actual linked SQLite version/features and repository-required runtime floor as separate facts; verify release policy against official runtime documentation before changing it.
Pin toolchain and dependency acquisition procedures, checksums and cache/offline behavior without silently updating dependency versions.
Distinguish missing tool, unsupported host, dependency-resolution failure, test failure and successful command execution.
Provide a fresh-environment bootstrap transcript reproducible by a second executor.
checks: An independent executor can build the recorded baseline using the recorded tools and lockfiles, or the exact missing capability is an unresolved blocker.
No downloaded toolchain, secret or cache directory is added to the source ZIP.
Compiler/runtime identity is attached to every later evidence bundle.

tasks.title: Run and classify the untouched baseline validation suite
steps: Run the repository-recorded formatting, locked Rust tests/build, protocol validator, TUI tests and installer/source-archive checks against the frozen snapshot.
Keep stdout, stderr, command argv, cwd, exit code, start/end times and source identity for every command, including failures.
Separate pure/unit, store, service, PTY-with-fixture, source packaging and installed-release evidence classes.
Reproduce candidate Rust compilation failures before making fixes; record failed tests whose expectations contradict M02 policy separately from implementation defects.
Run harness self-tests to determine whether a nonzero child exit or skipped platform check can be masked.
Produce a prioritized baseline defect list with minimal reproductions and affected future task IDs; do not mutate production code in this task.
checks: All attempted commands have durable results; missing tools and timeouts are not green.
Any baseline failing expectation is preserved and linked to a contract decision or defect task before it is changed.
The evidence report makes no product or release acceptance claim from this run alone.

tasks.title: Inventory public routes, verticals and source findings
steps: Enumerate registered service/CLI routes, aliases, version/capability fields, TUI actions and trusted workflow references from actual code.
Distinguish declared DTOs, persistence groundwork, wired application operations, public routes and validated user workflows.
Revisit F01-F22 and the architecture-review findings against the fresh files; classify confirmed-by-source, reproduced, no-longer-applicable or unresolved.
Record that update/upgrade routes and v3 groundwork exist without promoting them to production support.
Map each known gap to the production plan and original M02 task IDs; identify omissions beyond status and TUI, including source, memory and recovery.
Publish a drift report for report-versus-source and spec-versus-code contradictions.
checks: Every registered route has a current implementation/validation disposition.
Each retained architectural finding has a precise source anchor or reproducible evidence and a downstream owner.
No scaffold is called complete merely because its type or command name exists.

tasks.title: Inventory legacy data, external inputs and platform ownership
steps: Locate only supplied v1 archives, representative exports, database/schema versions and historical commands; do not assume historical absolute paths exist.
Hash available raw sources and classify which are safe read-only inputs, secrets requiring redaction, or absent evidence.
Request missing legacy records and supported macOS/Linux executors through the coordinator with exact required capability and downstream gate.
Record source completeness for work, dependencies, reviews, failed receipts, overrides, attempts, reservations, summaries and memory references.
Distinguish completing an inventory from proving full v1 parity; missing originals remain external blockers for migration/cutover.
Name independent-review and publication/signing authority requirements without fabricating people, approvals or credentials.
checks: The external-input register marks every item available, missing, restricted or not applicable with a reason.
No absent v1 behavior is silently replaced by an invented sample or by the v2 command registry.
PF-S12 and final cutover retain an explicit blocking link to unresolved retained legacy parity.

tasks.title: Set up isolated dispatch, evidence and shared-file integration
steps: Adopt the plan ID namespace and create a coordinator-owned task ledger with source revision, prerequisites, agent, reviewer and exclusive paths.
Assign separate worktrees and evidence/output directories; prohibit workers from sharing an uncommitted source tree or one live test project.
Implement a shared-file change-request process for crate roots, schemas, lockfiles, registries, protocol identities and installer/release generators.
Define accepted task, sprint review, reconciliation and revalidation as distinct states; independent reviewers cannot approve their own implementation.
Specify heartbeat/stop/reassignment handling for human-dispatched subagents; Markdown does not enforce runtime leases.
Validate the task graph and write-lock conflicts before the first dispatch; keep all current work not_started until explicitly assigned.
checks: Two workers cannot hold intersecting effective write sets or modify one shared manifest simultaneously.
A timed-out worker is stopped and its worktree inspected before replacement receives the same boundary.
A worker handoff alone cannot close a sprint or approve a release.

tasks.title: Produce the baseline-to-plan reconciliation and entry packet
steps: Reconcile baseline tests, known source defects, missing inputs and existing M01/M02 obligations into one immutable entry packet.
Preserve all 48 M02 task IDs and their historical unaccepted status; map each to future task coverage without marking it done.
List which architecture recommendations amend D22/D27, the bounded cycle strategy or protocol version and must be explicitly approved in PF-S01.
Identify baseline repair work necessary to enable testing and assign it to bounded future implementation tasks, never to the auditor.
Record known scope limits and the production-ready definition as proposed until the contract gate accepts it.
Hand the packet to an independent reviewer with exact source/evidence hashes and open questions.
checks: No old accepted/failed history is rewritten to fit the new plan.
Every baseline defect, missing input and mandatory M02 obligation has a target task or explicit blocking disposition.
The packet is sufficient for a new agent to identify the correct snapshot without chat history.

tasks.title: Freeze launch scope, authority boundaries and terminology
steps: Define production-ready for the approved local macOS/Linux, same-host, project-scoped product, including CLI/TUI/source/memory/no-goal agent workflows.
Document domain policy, application orchestration, transactional persistence, transport, projections and client ownership with allowed dependency directions.
Define planning identity, execution ownership and accepted outcome as distinct concepts; distinguish releasing an assignment from publishing software.
List approved non-goals and retained legacy obligations; do not expand to remote coordination, a web console or automatic harness launching.
Specify whether offline maintenance is supported and require the same application policy under an exclusive maintenance boundary.
Create a user-facing vocabulary map for complete/closed, expiry recovery, corruption, unavailable and explicit exceptions.
checks: Every core outcome has one authoritative owner and a supported public path.
No acceptance requirement relies on a TUI lifecycle engine, workflow prose authority or direct client SQLite access.
Non-goals do not defer core source/memory, guided work or isolation.

tasks.title: Freeze identity, revisions, operation outcomes and actor threat model
steps: Define project identity, workspace binding, database instance/restore epoch, service instance, authenticated principal, actor role, session and delegation.
Separate project snapshot revision, entity revision, proof-relevant revision and attempt fence; list exactly what increments or invalidates each.
Specify credential provisioning, rotation, revocation, role changes and local OS trust limits; caller-provided role or actor ID is not authentication.
Define operation ID scope, immutable request digest, accepted/rejected/pending/unknown outcomes, request deadlines and authoritative readback after timeout.
Explain when a not-found readback is definitive and when an original request can still commit; prohibit blind duplicate mutation.
Record multi-process same-user adversary limitations and enforceable filesystem/socket boundaries without claiming protection from unrestricted database edits.
checks: Wrong actor, foreign project, stale entity revision, stale proof revision, stale fence and restored database produce distinct contract cases.
A second session for the same principal cannot satisfy review independence by renaming itself.
Every mutating endpoint has a caller identity and durable operation-outcome rule.

tasks.title: Choose cycle-backed sprints and container acceptance
steps: Resolve the recommended task-to-milestone decomposition plus separate cycle assignment model against the current fixed tree and approved compatibility facade.
Define legacy sprint ID mappings and how work create --kind sprint routes to one cycle authority without duplicate mutable records.
Freeze cycle planned/active/completed/cancelled transitions, live-assignment cardinality, commitment revision and atomic carry-over dispositions.
Define milestone scope revisions and container accepted-closeout versus executable integration tasks; do not fabricate container execution attempts.
Separate task acceptance percentage from reconciled commitment percentage, including cancelled/deferred/replaced work.
Specify migration/rollback behavior and record explicit owner approval or a blocking alternative design before implementation proceeds.
checks: A carried-over task keeps its task identity and milestone parent with linked assignment history.
Two parallel cycles and cross-cycle dependencies are representable without treating cycles as executable proof subjects.
A rejected recommendation produces a revised versioned plan, not a worker-selected fallback.

tasks.title: Resolve execution budget, sealed submissions and safe ownership release
steps: Compare current D22/D27 end-to-end completion deadline with the recommended lease/hard-execution-budget plus sealed-submission model.
Choose explicitly whether human review consumes the hard budget; preserve the two-hour default unless the owner approves a versioned replacement.
Define how finish seals source/config/profile/proof context, when execution ownership ends, and what physical-stop evidence is required.
Define immutable submission validity, supersession, new execution attempts, review waiting and finalization without reusing a stale fence.
Specify manual adoption of externally performed work as an auditable session/attempt operation, never a shortcut for fabricated receipts.
Freeze cancellation request versus confirmed stop, release/fail/retry and durable expiry-disposition obligations.
checks: A long human review cannot accidentally be treated as a live executor or silently escape the chosen deadline policy.
At a deadline boundary, old execution authority is invalid even if no sweeper has run.
The owner approval names D22/D27 impact, migration and required conformance vectors.

tasks.title: Freeze status precedence, integrity axes and permitted actions
steps: Publish exact canonical predicates and tie-breaking order for terminal, unresolved expiry, intervention, draft, execution/submission gates, pause, retry, schedule, queued and ready.
Keep transport availability and record integrity separate from task status; define safe terminal-trust conditions and degraded evidence availability.
Preserve normal prerequisite waiting as queued; distinguish failed/missing/stale technical proof, rejected review, hard holds and operator-only claim policy.
Decide whether scheduled requires status/3 and define older-client behavior; do not add an enum silently to status/2.
Define structured primary and secondary reasons, stable priority/subject ordering, next reevaluation time and actor-specific allowed/denied actions.
Specify safe stop/release/recovery actions that remain available under a hard hold without authorizing forward progress.
checks: Every status has a positive, negative and combined-condition example plus a permitted-action table.
Identical canonical facts, actor context, policy version and as_of yield identical output.
Due dates add overdue information without extending or stealing execution authority.

tasks.title: Freeze profiles, proof selection and independent review policy
steps: Define immutable content-addressed profile versions and pinned per-work requirements independently of observed gate rows.
Resolve summary versus audit terminology and distinguish checkpoint, verification, review and closeout stages rather than renaming fields mechanically.
Specify relevant-evidence selection by complete subject/source/config/policy context before recency, deterministic ordering and explicit supersession rules.
Define authenticated executor attestation, cryptographic artifact identity, required observables and supported verifier command policy.
Specify review roles, principal/delegation independence, approve/reject/return/revoke semantics, and which decisions create hard reconciliation obligations.
Define what changes stale proof, review and close intent; optional gates must never unexpectedly become mandatory.
checks: Deleting a gate observation cannot delete the requirement.
A rejected review remains different from missing review in every read/action decision.
A newer unrelated receipt cannot shadow valid current-subject evidence; stale or altered evidence cannot satisfy proof.

tasks.title: Freeze dependency, reopen and override truth-preservation rules
steps: Choose allowed execution-edge endpoint kinds, recommended task-to-task accepted-close prerequisites, and separate container ordering relations.
Define atomic cycle detection, edge identity, terminal edge edits, cross-project rejection and accepted-outcome binding.
Specify prerequisite reopen/revocation effects on new claims, active successors and historically closed successors without recursively rewriting history.
Define typed gate exception and edge waiver records with principal, permission, reason, comment, target revision, scope, evidence and validity interval.
Define revocation/expiry effects on future use versus previously committed acceptance; preserve failed raw proof and unmet edges visibly.
Specify cancellation/defer/replacement disposition and reject any override that purports to fix corruption, foreign identity or a stale executor fence.
checks: Only accepted closed satisfies the default dependency policy.
A waiver affects one approved edge/version and never fabricates an upstream accepted result.
Every reopen/override has a deterministic impact preview and explicit audit/readback requirement.

tasks.title: Freeze protocol, external jobs and compatibility evolution
steps: Define versioned request/response envelopes for commands, snapshot reads, action descriptors, diagnostics, cursors and operation readback.
Specify unknown-outcome, busy, revision-conflict, forbidden, expired, corrupt and incompatible errors with retry rules that cannot duplicate writes.
Require all mutation authorization within a transaction over current canonical facts; candidate queries and client affordances are hints only.
Define durable external-job stages for verifier processes, Git publication, backups and update activation, including crash-after-side-effect readback.
Set schema/API/status/workflow/memory identity negotiation and N/N-1 compatibility policy; unknown enums cannot be silently coerced.
Specify bounded response size, pagination consistency, reconnect gap recovery, maintenance mode and one-service election ownership.
checks: Every intended public route maps to one application use case and typed schema.
Timeout can never be reported as certain rejection without authoritative evidence.
Version upgrades name supported/unsupported combinations and do not make new clients reconstruct missing lifecycle policy.

tasks.title: Set security, resource, support and release acceptance budgets
steps: Name supported platform/architecture combinations and installation modes based on actual intended release ownership; keep Windows/remote hosting out of scope unless explicitly approved.
Set measured performance and resource acceptance budgets before optimization: dashboard latency, queue wait, transaction hold, heartbeat fairness, memory, history growth and disconnect recovery.
Define source/receipt limits, process-tree cleanup, symlink/path handling, secret redaction, credential storage and audit access controls.
Choose artifact authentication/signing, checksum provenance, dependency audit policy, linked-runtime policy and release reproducibility expectations.
Define backup consistency across database/blobs/Git, supported rollback boundaries, restore identity revocation and RPO/RTO acceptance experiments.
Record benchmark hardware/workload/environment and forbid adjusting thresholds after a failed run without an independently reviewed contract change.
checks: No release-required platform or security budget remains an unnamed future check.
Repository SQLite floor is an explicit packaging gate to verify on each actual artifact, not a factual claim that development runtime meets it.
Critical integrity/isolation/authority failures are nonwaivable.

tasks.title: Freeze source, curated memory and retained legacy parity contracts
steps: Define supported source intake kinds, immutable version identities, parser-failure retention, citation locators and project-local retrieval filters.
Define live notes/drafts versus Git-published curated memory, publisher authority and recoverable publication/reimport states.
Bind handoff context to exact work/submission/source revisions and clarify that source content cannot become trusted directives.
Map all known retained v1 behaviors into the new contract with preserve/rework/replace/defer/historical-only dispositions.
Carry absent v1 inputs from the baseline register into explicit migration acceptance blockers; contract drafting must not pretend the original records were inspected.
Define memory/source backup, garbage-collection roots and source-edit/policy-change proof invalidation semantics.
checks: Core source/memory and no-goal guidance cannot disappear behind a scope simplification.
Historical complete/done vocabulary is not sufficient evidence of accepted v2 closed.
Every source-derived claim and published memory entry can point to preserved project-scoped provenance.

tasks.title: Integrate versioned contracts, conformance oracle and plan amendment
steps: Collect signed/attributable owner decisions and merge contract drafts through one serialized steward, preserving prior decisions and explicit supersession links.
Record formal adoption of this finer-grained dispatch graph; explain the intentional early isolation work and which original M02 gates are expanded, not silently bypassed.
Create a conformance oracle mapping each invariant to legal, illegal, boundary, race and restart vectors, including status/action combinations.
Update contract/schema/protocol/workflow identities together without relabeling incompatible fixtures as compatible.
Link unresolved external legacy/platform inputs to their blocking future acceptance tasks while confirming no implementation depends on an unapproved semantic decision.
Validate all references, route names, schemas, task DAG and independent review assignments before releasing the contract candidate.
checks: No implementation task is dispatchable while one of its semantic decision prerequisites is unresolved.
All 48 M02 obligations have explicit coverage and no historical gate is fabricated.
The contract validator detects version drift and missing required scenarios rather than accepting a hand-edited success label.

tasks.title: Implement ordered schema migration and invariant verification
steps: Translate the accepted contract into versioned additive/rebuild migrations with checksums, a ledger and explicit pre/postconditions.
Verify current schema identity and unsupported newer versions before opening the service for mutations.
Run each migration within a supported transaction or documented staged recovery protocol; never update the version marker before durable success.
Preserve the supplied v2/v3 baseline and legacy rows; map malformed or ambiguous rows into diagnostics instead of inventing valid values.
Implement concurrent-open migration exclusion and interrupted-migration recovery without force-breaking a live service lock.
Add fresh-create, upgrade, repeated-open, failed-step rollback and compatibility rejection cases.
checks: An interrupted migration never leaves a false schema version or partially accepted canonical relation.
A second service cannot operate on a database mid-migration.
Every preexisting record is preserved, explicitly transformed with provenance, or rejected with an actionable report.

tasks.title: Create bounded store module seams for parallel implementation
steps: Extract only the store transaction/profile/execution/operation/acceptance seams required by later tasks; preserve public behavior and avoid a framework rewrite.
Move shared decoding and transaction ownership helpers to one named location so nested BEGIN calls and duplicated policy are not introduced.
Define internal storage request/result interfaces from the frozen contract and expose registration points for later modules.
Keep domain evaluation in Rust domain/application; do not translate status authorization into a second SQL predicate.
Run baseline and focused tests before and after the extraction and explain any mechanically necessary API adjustments.
Publish exact new-file ownership and root-module integration requests so execution and evidence agents can work without editing the monolith concurrently.
checks: The same baseline cases produce the same outcomes before and after extraction apart from explicitly reviewed compile repairs.
All new module registrations compile on the combined tree; disconnected code files cannot close this task.
Later tasks have actual disjoint write seams, not imaginary function-level locks inside one file.

tasks.title: Persist project, database, entity and proof revision identities
steps: Persist project ID, database instance/restore epoch and validated workspace-binding metadata according to the contract.
Implement distinct project snapshot, entity, proof and attempt-fence types at storage boundaries with checked conversions.
Define which semantic writes advance proof/entity/project revisions and which liveness writes do not invalidate unrelated work.
Enforce project-scoped composite references and prevent a foreign project ID from being paired with local child IDs.
Migrate old conflated revisions explicitly, preserving provenance and revoking ambiguous outstanding operation contexts where required.
Return typed conflict details with current relevant revision without leaking foreign project state.
checks: A heartbeat on task A does not spuriously invalidate a proof-bound review on unrelated task B.
Wrong project/database epoch and stale entity/proof/fence values are independently rejected.
Restore cannot resurrect an old pending operation or execution authority.

tasks.title: Persist immutable acceptance profiles and pinned requirements
steps: Store complete canonical profile definitions, immutable version identifiers and a real content digest independently of gate observations.
Resolve per-work pinned required/optional gate declarations at publication and persist their definition/version provenance.
Reject conflicting content under an existing profile/version rather than ignoring it with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING.
Define task and container acceptance requirement storage according to their distinct subjects.
Handle legacy empty definitions through explicit reconstruction only when authoritative provenance exists; otherwise quarantine claim/close with a repair path.
Ensure gate/result deletion or drift is detectable from the independent declaration set.
checks: Deleting a required observed gate produces a configuration/integrity gap, never fewer requirements.
Changing a profile default does not silently change existing pinned tasks.
Two sibling tasks can retain different profile versions and gate requirements after reopen/restart.

tasks.title: Persist submissions, reviews, accepted outcomes and exceptions
steps: Implement the approved submission or equivalent proof-context identity, including work proof revision, attempt/fence, source/config/profile and supersession.
Persist append-only review decisions as typed outcomes, including rejected/returned/revoked, without reducing them to a boolean.
Persist durable close intents and accepted-outcome records binding exact satisfied requirements and explicit exception IDs.
Persist typed gate exceptions and edge waivers with scope, revision, principal, reason, comment, evidence and validity state.
Add immutable receipt/artifact references with subject constraints and deterministic ordering metadata.
Provide storage reads that preserve old decisions and failed observations while identifying the current applicable context.
checks: A rejected review is round-tripped without becoming absent/open review.
Raw failure and an exception that permits acceptance remain independently queryable.
Accepted outcome identity survives ending an execution lease and cannot be forged by setting lifecycle alone.

tasks.title: Persist durable recovery, resource ownership and external jobs
steps: Store expiry/failure/uncertain-stop obligations independently of current-attempt pointers with subject, fence, reason and resolution history.
Store resource/worktree reservations and release acknowledgements so ownership cannot be reassigned while a process may still write.
Define durable job records for external verifier/Git/backup/update stages with idempotency keys and expected-side-effect readback.
Enforce one current execution per task and session plus approved resource overlap constraints at the database level.
Preserve all terminal attempts and recovery decisions; no sweep may erase the need for disposition.
Support bounded queries for unresolved obligations and active jobs without scanning all historical attempts.
checks: Clearing current_attempt cannot make expired work ready while its recovery obligation remains unresolved.
Duplicate live ownership is rejected transactionally even when application checks race.
A crash after an external effect leaves a resumable/reconcilable job, not a guessed successful state.

tasks.title: Persist command registration, outcomes and audit atomically
steps: Implement scoped operation registration with immutable caller/command/target/request-digest identity and accepted request lifetime.
Commit semantic mutations, outcome and audit event atomically; persist attributable validation/rejection outcomes without unintended target changes.
Reject replay with changed payload, actor, project or database epoch; exact replay returns the stored outcome.
Represent pending/unknown side effects separately from terminal rejected/succeeded operations.
Add bounded indexed history/readback and redaction-safe audit details without logging credentials or unbounded receipt bodies.
Define failure behavior when durable audit/outcome persistence itself fails: do not acknowledge a successful canonical mutation without its required records.
checks: Crash after commit-before-response resolves to one original committed outcome and one audit event.
A rejected action records its disposition while leaving prohibited canonical fields unchanged.
Operation IDs cannot be reused to cross an actor/project boundary or change payload.

tasks.title: Implement corruption-tolerant canonical decoding and scope quarantine
steps: Decode canonical numeric clocks, IDs, lifecycle, parent kinds, profiles, reviews and dependency endpoints with typed diagnostic results.
Separate unreadable row diagnostics from project-wide unsafe identity/schema failures.
Replace fail-all prefetch behavior with scoped relation diagnostics where it is safe to identify affected work; do not drop unreadable prerequisites.
Propagate unsafe ancestry/requirements to dependent actions while preserving valid unrelated siblings and exact diagnostic counts.
Make accepted-outcome trust checks explicit; malformed terminal rows cannot automatically satisfy prerequisites.
Provide read-only diagnostic detail and repair preconditions without silently mutating or synthesizing records during reads.
checks: One damaged review/profile/attempt row does not crash an otherwise safely readable project snapshot.
A dependent never becomes ready because a prerequisite could not be decoded.
Unsafe project identity or schema quarantines the full appropriate scope and cannot be overridden by a UI label.

tasks.title: Integrate storage invariants with fresh/upgrade/rollback tests
steps: Run all new relations through one real SQLite database opened by the supported store, not a mocked persistence trait.
Exercise unique constraints, foreign references, operation replay and row quarantine in fresh and upgraded v2/v3 databases.
Inject failures between migration and transaction steps in disposable projects; retain before/after hashes and invariants.
Verify all module/root/schema registrations on the integrated source and update compatibility manifests through the steward.
Record performance-sensitive indexes/query plans without claiming service-scale success yet.
Hand the exact combined source and schema identity to independent storage review.
checks: Fresh creation and supported upgrades expose the same accepted storage contract.
No failure scenario loses historical records, permits cross-project references or reports a partial migration as accepted.
All downstream storage APIs compile together and their domain-policy ownership remains explicit.

tasks.title: Introduce typed decision inputs and proof-relevant identities
steps: Define canonical fact types for lifecycle, actor authority, pinned requirements, dependency outcomes, holds, execution, submissions, reviews and unresolved recovery.
Use distinct newtypes for entity/proof revisions and fences with no transport/storage/JSON dependencies.
Represent absent, unreadable, stale and explicitly failed facts distinctly; do not encode all as None or false.
Model evaluated-at and next-change timestamps through an injected clock value.
Define typed integrity scope and permitted-action inputs independently of transport availability.
Publish pure test builders for valid and invalid canonical fact combinations without using them as service acceptance receipts.
checks: Malformed and contradictory inputs produce explicit diagnostics rather than accidentally valid defaults.
The domain compiles without store/service/process/TUI imports.
A field named revision cannot be substituted for a fence or unrelated revision type.

tasks.title: Implement exhaustive status precedence and reason ordering
steps: Collect all applicable facts before selecting the primary status; implement the frozen precedence including the expiry-versus-hard-hold tie.
Keep primary_reason explicit and preserve secondary reasons by stable priority, subject and code without collapsing different prerequisites.
Represent ordinary dependency waiting as queued, explicit pause/retry as policy states and operator-only as actor-specific eligibility.
Handle active execution, current submission verification/review and closeout-pending semantics according to the accepted budget/submission decision.
Reject invalid terminal acceptance identity or malformed requirement context through integrity output, not false ready/closed.
Provide explanatory next-safe-action inputs without embedding human text as policy.
checks: Paused plus prerequisite returns paused with both reasons; expiry plus hold preserves both and the selected tie rule.
Failed proof, rejected review and missing review never collapse into one outcome.
Repeated evaluation and permutation of equivalent unordered facts produce byte-equivalent semantic decisions.

tasks.title: Implement exact clock, schedule, retry and expiry predicates
steps: Implement lease renewal, immutable hard budget, retry not-before, scheduled eligibility and due/overdue as separate predicates.
Define at-deadline comparison and expired authority even when persistence has not yet materialized an expiry job.
Exclude historical failed/released/cancelled attempt clocks from current ownership while retaining unresolved recovery obligations.
Compute next reevaluation time from relevant timers, exception validity and schedule boundaries.
Handle validated wall-clock discontinuity/restart policy without silently granting extra hard budget.
Implement deterministic bounded backoff inputs without random policy divergence across readers.
checks: At the exact deadline, stale execution cannot mutate; a late timer does not extend authority.
Overdue changes information but not lease ownership or accepted outcome.
A terminal historical attempt with an old deadline cannot incorrectly expire an idle task without a current recovery obligation.

tasks.title: Implement requirement, evidence and review interpretation
steps: Compare pinned requirement declarations against observed gates and reject missing, duplicate, mistyped or wrong-version definitions.
Filter proof by the complete accepted subject context before deterministic recency/supersession selection.
Preserve missing, failed, stale, altered and irrelevant proof as different reasoned outcomes.
Evaluate typed review decisions with required principal independence and policy-defined rejection/return effects.
Compute effective requirement satisfaction through valid typed exceptions while preserving raw unsatisfied observations.
Distinguish task proof, container scope acceptance and closeout-summary requirements without synthesizing attempts for containers.
checks: Unrelated newer evidence is inert with respect to current proof validity.
A forced failed gate is effectively excepted but still visibly failed with the exception ID.
A deleted declaration/result mismatch and a self-review both fail closed with distinct reasons.

tasks.title: Implement dependency satisfaction, graph and reopen impact rules
steps: Implement allowed endpoint kinds, duplicate/self-edge rejection, cycle validation and project-scope predicates.
Satisfy default edges only from trustworthy accepted-closed outcome identity; complete/verified/cancelled remain unsatisfied.
Apply only current edge-specific waivers and return unmet raw prerequisite plus exception context.
Compute reopen/revocation impact for pending, active and historically closed successors without mutating historical facts in a pure evaluator.
Separate planning ordering relations and cycle assignments from executable prerequisite semantics.
Define deterministic affected-subgraph output for mutation authorization and user impact previews.
checks: A cancelled or reopened prerequisite cannot satisfy a new default claim merely because an old label says closed.
Cross-project, cyclic and policy-incompatible edges are rejected.
The same graph represented in different insertion orders yields the same satisfaction and impact results.

tasks.title: Implement explicit authorization and allowed-action decisions
steps: Define action-specific predicates for publish/claim/accept/start/checkpoint/evidence/finish/review/close/stop/release/pause/resume/cancel/reopen and exceptions.
Evaluate authenticated principal role/delegation, entity/proof revision, fence, current facts and target scope independently of display label.
Return allowed actions with required inputs/confirmation semantics and denied actions with stable causes and safe recovery routes.
Ensure holds prevent prohibited forward progress while allowing policy-approved stop, readback, history and reconciliation operations.
Do not let an operator override bypass corrupt identity, stale fences or foreign projects.
Provide one action-decision interface used by mutation transactions and read projections.
checks: The same blocked task can deny claim/close while allowing a safe authorized stop request.
A ready task may deny this actor without becoming a globally blocked task.
No adapter must infer permission from a status string or gate count.

tasks.title: Implement container scope and cycle rollup primitives
steps: Define pure task-count and container/cycle rollup inputs over a named scope/assignment revision.
Compute accepted outcomes, reconciled dispositions, active executions, gate/review gaps, overdue work and actionable blockers separately.
Keep cancelled/deferred/replaced commitments out of successful-work numerators while accounting for reconciled scope.
Expose incomplete/unknown totals when the scope cannot be safely decoded; never use a page count as total.
Define container close readiness from descendant accepted outcomes and explicit dispositions, plus optional integration closeout task.
Make provisional container_planning/non_executable_container placeholders unnecessary without making containers claimable.
checks: A cycle with deferred tasks reports reconciled scope without claiming those tasks succeeded.
A container with normal queued work does not appear as a hard-blocked executable task.
Corrupt descendants cannot create a misleading 100 percent accepted rollup.

tasks.title: Add property, differential and exhaustive transition tests
steps: Generate valid/invalid fact combinations from the frozen oracle and compare every status/action to the normative table.
Test idempotence, stable reason ordering, historical-evidence invariance, isolation, exact deadlines and accepted-outcome dependency rules.
Test terminal stability unless an explicit reopen/impact decision is present; do not assert that terminal states can never legally change.
Exercise every legal/illegal transition pair and multiple concurrent-condition combinations.
Use shrinking/minimal counterexamples and preserve failing seeds and input cases as evidence.
Compare legacy candidate behaviors only to identify deltas, not to redefine the approved contract.
checks: Every normative reason/status/action rule has positive and negative coverage.
A deliberately removed requirement, rejected review or timer predicate causes a test failure.
Property results identify exact source/policy version and do not claim store/service integration.

tasks.title: Integrate one public domain decision API and remove duplicate policy
steps: Export a single canonical decision/action API and approved fact types through the domain crate root.
Audit remaining helper evaluators for semantic duplication; retire them or make them delegate to the canonical functions.
Provide typed integration examples to store/application owners without editing their policy locally.
Document required snapshot facts, error behavior and absence versus corruption semantics.
Run full domain tests and compile adapter consumers on the integrated branch to catch incompatible signatures early.
Record source search evidence that no writable display-status mutation API was introduced.
checks: There is one normative predicate implementation for each status/action/acceptance rule.
Consumers receive a complete API and migration guidance rather than disconnected modules.
The independent domain reviewer can reproduce conformance without storage or terminal concerns.

tasks.title: Implement explicit project initialization and workspace binding
steps: Resolve the selected project from the working directory or explicit selector, with no fallback to a prior/global project.
Make initialization explicit and validate project ID, database instance and canonical workspace binding before exposing any data.
Reject absent, stale, foreign, malformed and mismatched metadata with typed run-init/rebind guidance.
Define move/restore/clone handling from the accepted contract: bind an existing identity only by an explicit authorized operation.
Prevent reading the database before selected-project identity is established; avoid foreign names in error/detail output.
Preserve existing setup UX where compatible and keep initialization idempotent without enrolling new privileged actors.
checks: Two temporary directories with overlapping IDs cannot read each other through implicit discovery.
A copied metadata file cannot silently select another project database.
Repeated initialization cannot become an actor-creation or role-escalation route.

tasks.title: Enforce resolved path, symlink and file-descriptor confinement
steps: Revalidate canonicalized database and workspace paths after lexical normalization; explicitly reject traversal and forbidden symlink targets.
Use descriptor-relative or equivalent platform-safe opening where needed to avoid checking one path and opening another after a race.
Apply the same selected-project policy to database sidecars, sockets, evidence blobs, gate files, source attachments, memory paths and backup destinations.
Define explicit authorized external paths separately from implicit project-local paths; do not silently broaden confinement to make tests pass.
Test symlink replacement, nested directories, spaces, non-ASCII names, moved roots and parent traversal on supported filesystems.
Document residual local-OS trust assumptions and avoid claiming protection from a process allowed to rewrite the database directly.
checks: A path that resolves outside the permitted project boundary is rejected even when its lexical prefix looks local.
A check/open race cannot redirect a protected operation to a foreign project target under the supported trust model.
Error messages are useful without disclosing contents of rejected foreign paths.

tasks.title: Implement credential-backed principals and safe bootstrap
steps: Implement the approved local credential/principal boundary, verification and project membership without trusting actor_id or role fields as proof.
Bind a one-time bootstrap operator to an explicit initialization authority and close enrollment afterward.
Separate actor creation, role assignment and credential issuance into permissioned auditable operations.
Resolve authoritative role/delegation inside the mutation context and make read capabilities reflect the authenticated principal.
Reject forged actor text, copied credentials outside authorized project scope, unknown/revoked credentials and stale authority versions.
Keep credentials out of logs, receipts, snapshots, source archives and user-visible diagnostics.
checks: Supplying role=operator or a known operator ID cannot elevate an agent.
Initialization of an existing project cannot create a privileged identity.
Authentication and role denial are distinguishable without revealing credential contents.

tasks.title: Bind sessions, delegation and review identity to principals
steps: Bind each session to an authenticated principal, harness identity, project, runtime identity and supported capability version.
Enforce one live execution per session while allowing an actor to have separately authorized sessions under explicit capacity rules.
Record delegation chain and effective permissions; prohibit delegated sessions from claiming independence from their original principal when policy forbids it.
Define session liveness separately from task progress and preserve ended/revoked session history.
Reject a different session silently adopting a live attempt; require the explicit recovery/adoption path.
Provide bounded actor/session context to action decisions without exposing secrets.
checks: Two sessions of one principal cannot bypass configured review independence.
Revoked or foreign sessions cannot heartbeat, finish or review another project execution.
Session restart/re-registration does not silently inherit a stale fence.

tasks.title: Implement role changes, credential revocation and authority audit
steps: Implement explicit role/delegation changes with reason, expected authority revision, actor identity and durable operation outcome.
Recheck authority at transaction time so revocation races cannot authorize a later mutation on a cached role.
Define what credential revocation does to active executions, pending operations and future review/publication actions under the approved policy.
Preserve historical attribution and already-committed decisions; do not delete principals referenced by audit/history.
Require a safe last-operator recovery procedure rather than accidentally removing all administrative access.
Provide readback and a minimally disclosed security audit of accepted and rejected changes.
checks: Role revocation racing with an override/close yields an outcome consistent with one serialized order.
Historical receipts/reviews retain their original principal after credential rotation.
No self-grant or unauthorized last-operator change is possible.

tasks.title: Protect service sockets, maintenance and local process authority
steps: Create private runtime directories and sockets with supported OS ownership/permission checks and project/database identity binding.
Authenticate/authorize transport requests before dispatch and validate the service instance during connection/reconnection.
Reject foreign or stale sockets and spoofed metadata without force-breaking a verified live owner.
Implement exclusive offline maintenance entry that uses the same application policy and cannot overlap a normal writer/service.
Bound unauthenticated request parsing, frame size and security logging to avoid denial-of-service amplification.
Test concurrent election, owner death, stale socket cleanup and malicious precreated paths on real local sockets.
checks: An unauthorized local caller cannot invoke project mutations merely by knowing the socket path.
Normal service and exclusive maintenance cannot write concurrently.
Stale cleanup never kills or steals ownership from a verified live service.

tasks.title: Enforce project scope across artifacts, source, memory and errors
steps: Audit all source/blob/memory/receipt/operation lookup APIs for project filtering and authorization, including indirect references.
Reject foreign artifact IDs and paths even when they exist locally or have the same content hash.
Scope caches, index keys, diagnostic details, operation readback and pagination cursors by project/database/authority identity.
Prevent source text or cited documents from injecting trusted command directives or changing project selection.
Define explicit export/import/grant as the only future cross-project transfer mechanism; do not introduce a global canonical registry.
Test overlapping IDs and identical hashes in two projects through read and mutation APIs.
checks: Project A cannot query or use Project B evidence, memory, operation outcomes or diagnostics.
Cached data is never considered authenticated merely because it was loaded earlier.
A foreign source attachment cannot become proof or guidance for a local task without an explicit permitted import.

tasks.title: Run independent isolation and authority penetration cases
steps: Drive real service routes with forged IDs/roles, revoked credentials, copied metadata, stale sockets and wrong project/database epochs.
Race reinit/enrollment, privilege revocation, session replacement and directory/symlink changes with protected operations.
Probe error envelopes, cached reads and operation readback for cross-project information leakage.
Test authorized success paths as controls; indiscriminately denying all actions is not acceptance.
Retain audit events and before/after selected-project snapshots as evidence, with credentials redacted.
Publish scope-qualified findings including any platform boundary the executor could not exercise.
checks: Every denied attack leaves prohibited canonical state unchanged and records the appropriate attributable outcome.
Authorized actors can still initialize/use/recover their own project.
Unexercised OS/platform cases remain blockers for supported targets, not passed fixtures.

tasks.title: Implement version negotiation and typed command/query envelopes
steps: Implement approved project/database/service identity, actor context, operation metadata and separated revision fields in DTOs.
Add structured status/integrity/reason/action/diagnostic responses and versioned compatibility behavior.
Represent accepted/rejected/conflict/busy/unknown/pending outcomes independently of transport response success.
Validate unknown fields/enums, unsupported versions, mismatched identity and response limits according to the frozen compatibility matrix.
Keep backward-readable fields only where semantics remain equivalent; reject an incompatible status/action contract rather than coercing it.
Update manifests and golden DTO examples via the single protocol steward and compile both Rust and TypeScript consumers.
checks: Old/new supported combinations decode with explicit compatibility behavior; unsupported combinations fail clearly.
A corrupt or contradictory primary reason/action descriptor is rejected, not repaired by a client.
Every mutation response contains enough scoped identity for safe readback.

tasks.title: Implement one application command executor and transaction contract
steps: Centralize authentication context, request validation, operation registration, transaction entry and domain action evaluation for supported mutations.
Reread target facts, authority, relevant dependencies, holds, requirements and timers inside the committing transaction.
Use expected entity/proof revision and fence for their actual meanings; do not compare a work revision to the global project clock.
Return typed current-state denial/readback without performing external process or Git work while holding the writer.
Ensure direct/offline CLI adapters use this executor under the same maintenance boundary rather than raw helper bypasses.
Integrate storage operation/outcome/audit commits and explicit rollback behavior for errors.
checks: A lower-level supported adapter cannot bypass a hold, stale fence, role restriction or missing requirement.
Rejected operations produce a durable attributable outcome without prohibited target changes.
A deliberate external sleep does not occur while the canonical write transaction is held.

tasks.title: Implement request admission, idempotency and definitive readback
steps: Persist request admission/expiry semantics sufficient to determine whether an original timed-out request may still commit.
Bind replay to project/database epoch, principal, command, target and request digest.
Expose operation status for pending, committed, rejected and unresolved cases with safe retry/readback advice.
Handle crash before admission, after admission, after canonical commit and after external side effect with durable reconciliation.
Reject a second payload under one operation ID and prevent an old request being admitted after a definitive expired/not-found outcome.
Avoid client-generated new IDs for automatic retry of the same uncertain mutation.
checks: Timeout-after-commit returns the original durable result when read back and never produces a second mutation.
Not found is called definitive only under the accepted admission/expiry protocol.
Operation polling cannot reveal outcomes belonging to a foreign principal/project.

tasks.title: Integrate production service host and single-writer queue
steps: Wire authenticated envelopes to the one application executor and durable operation lifecycle in the production host.
Bound queue capacity, request memory, wait time and cancellation handling with typed busy/outcome semantics.
Apply approved fairness across heartbeat, operator recovery, planning and ordinary work without allowing starvation.
Measure queue wait, transaction hold and external-job time separately; do not label the whole latency as database time.
Ensure request cancellation before commit has an explicit outcome and cancellation after commit remains readback-safe.
Preserve one elected service writer plus consistent reader connections per project.
checks: Overload returns bounded typed responses without duplicate commits or lost operations.
Long verification does not monopolize the writer queue.
Concurrent service startups cannot create independent authoritative writers.

tasks.title: Assemble canonical reads and server-owned action descriptors
steps: Assemble required facts from immutable declarations and typed recovery/review records, not from current-attempt or boolean shortcuts.
Evaluate status, secondary reasons, timers and action permissions through the single domain decision API.
Return allowed and denied actions with required inputs, relevant revision, confirmation scope and recovery links.
Keep per-row integrity and connection availability separate; do not invent normal statuses for unreadable work.
Return snapshot/project identity so CLI/TUI/guidance can compare only like-for-like results.
Add read-versus-transaction equivalence tests for the same facts and actor, allowing expected change only when the transaction snapshot advances.
checks: Read eligibility and mutation authorization agree for identical canonical facts and evaluation time.
A rejected review remains intervention and a durable expiry obligation survives an absent current attempt.
The TUI can render all action enablement without computing lifecycle rules.

tasks.title: Implement revision-consistent pagination and subscription recovery
steps: Publish revision notifications only after committed canonical changes and include scoped project/database/service identity.
Bind cursors, filters, totals and pages to a consistent snapshot or return an explicit stale-cursor restart requirement.
Detect notification gaps, reconnects and restored-database epochs; require a full resync rather than applying speculative patches.
Coalesce noisy liveness notifications without losing semantic updates or changing proof revisions.
Bound subscription buffers and slow-client behavior with observable resynchronization.
Keep source/index lag separate from canonical project revision and report it explicitly.
checks: Paging while writes occur never mixes counts and rows from incompatible snapshots without a typed stale response.
A disconnected client converges from a new snapshot after a gap.
A late Project A event cannot be accepted by a Project B subscription.

tasks.title: Implement durable external-job scheduling and readback hooks
steps: Schedule external work only from committed job intents with scoped identity and idempotency keys.
Provide start/observe/complete/reconcile hooks for verifier, Git publication, maintenance and update workers without encoding their product policy in transport.
Record job ownership/heartbeat/result independently from task execution ownership.
Reconcile crash-after-side-effect through artifact/commit/process readback; do not rerun a non-idempotent effect blindly.
Bound job concurrency, output retention and cancellation acknowledgement.
Ensure recovery jobs cannot grant a new work fence or overwrite a committed accepted outcome by themselves.
checks: Job restart preserves the original identity and produces at most one accepted result under the configured side-effect protocol.
An uncertain external effect remains visibly pending/reconciling.
The database writer is released before subprocess, Git or filesystem-heavy work begins.

tasks.title: Add genuine service harness and negative proof controls
steps: Start the actual built service in disposable project/runtime directories and record absolute binary path/hash, protocol/schema/runtime identity and process IDs.
Create test work and invoke operations through supported routes; do not seed successful receipts or dashboard rows directly.
Provide deterministic test clock/fault controls only through an explicitly restricted test build or owned harness boundary, never an unauthenticated production bypass.
Capture commands, requests, responses, operation readback, artifact hashes and invariant checks as reusable evidence.
Add canary negative cases proving the harness fails on nonzero verifier exit, wrong project, fake receipt, stale fence and missing review.
Support cleanup after interruption without killing unrelated processes or deleting source/legacy data.
checks: A deliberately broken lifecycle invariant makes the harness fail rather than echo fixture success.
All success evidence originates from actual service-visible operations and executed verification.
Harness cleanup is isolated, and unavailable sockets/platforms remain reported limitations.

tasks.title: Integrate and test all service/direct/maintenance adapter boundaries
steps: Inventory every supported direct, socket and maintenance mutation route and map it to the canonical application executor.
Remove or fence raw helper paths that permit a production adapter to mutate without authentication/revision/policy/audit checks.
Run the same positive and denied operation vectors through each supported route.
Verify compatibility, identity, error and unknown-outcome behavior on the combined source.
Record explicit unavailable routes as pending CLI/planning work rather than exposing partial capabilities as complete.
Prepare service contract handoffs for execution, evidence, planning, source/memory and UI consumers.
checks: All supported adapters converge on the same domain and transactional rules.
No unavailable future route is advertised as an accepted capability.
The service sprint is validated against the actual production host, not only trait mocks.

tasks.title: Implement transactional claim and accepted execution context
steps: Select bounded ready candidates as hints and reread all authorization/requirements/dependency/recovery facts inside the final claim transaction.
Bind authenticated principal/session, entity revision, current accepted prerequisites, worktree/resource request and execution policy.
Create one attempt, reservation, fence, renewable lease and approved hard budget with operation/audit outcome atomically.
Return exact acceptance requirements, source/workspace constraints, deadlines and next permitted action.
Reject hold, pause, retry/schedule, wrong actor, missing requirement, unresolved recovery and conflicting execution/resource ownership.
Preserve deterministic ordering for automatic candidate selection without adding automatic harness launching.
checks: Competing claimers yield one accepted owner and typed losers with no duplicate reservation.
A displayed blocked/queued/paused/expired task cannot be claimed through any lower-level supported route.
No claim is authorized from a stale candidate query alone.

tasks.title: Implement accept/start and session-bound runtime identity
steps: Implement claimed-to-accepted-to-running transitions with current fence, session, deadlines and action policy inside the transaction.
Record immutable harness/toolchain/protocol/source workspace identity at acceptance according to the contract.
Reject foreign sessions, stale fences, incompatible runtimes and acceptance after expiration.
Make duplicate accept/start with the same operation identity idempotent; changed payload is a conflict.
Keep runtime process launch observation outside the transaction and record unknown start outcomes explicitly.
Return current phase, remaining authority and evidence requirements without treating acceptance as useful progress.
checks: An unaccepted expired claim cannot be revived by a late accept.
A second session cannot start someone else’s attempt.
Crash/retry of accept/start does not create a second runtime ownership episode.

tasks.title: Implement worktree/resource reservation and safe adoption
steps: Implement isolated worktree or approved explicit resource/write-set reservations with canonical project path checks.
Reject overlapping unsafe writers even when they claim different tasks; keep database and filesystem ownership responsibilities distinct.
Provide a manual adoption path for an already-running harness or human work with authenticated actor, explicit source state and no invented past execution evidence.
Record process/host/session identity and stop-observation provenance sufficient for safe resource release.
Require reconciliation when a prior owner may still write; an expired database fence alone is insufficient.
Define clean/dirty worktree handoff and preservation of uncommitted user/agent changes without destructive resets.
checks: Two different tasks cannot concurrently write one protected resource under incompatible ownership.
A replacement is denied while the previous process is unconfirmed or still writing.
Manual adoption is audited and cannot fabricate prior passing receipts or claim independence.

tasks.title: Implement heartbeat and durable checkpoint semantics
steps: Renew only the permitted lease using authenticated current-fence/session authority; never extend the hard budget through heartbeat.
Record liveness/tool/process information separately from semantic checkpoint/progress events.
Validate checkpoint source/attempt references and retain blockers, partial results and safe next action.
Bound checkpoint size, heartbeat frequency, history noise and queue pressure.
Return exact expiry and next-renewal information without conflating a healthy long-running tool with stalled progress.
Test duplicate and reordered heartbeats/checkpoints across service restart.
checks: A heartbeat cannot change the hard execution/completion deadline or unrelated proof revision.
Healthy work without file changes remains live without manufacturing progress.
An old/revoked session cannot renew or write a checkpoint for replacement ownership.

tasks.title: Implement exact expiry and durable unresolved disposition
steps: Enforce expiry on reads and mutations at the exact lease/hard-budget boundary even before the scheduled job runs.
Materialize an idempotent durable recovery obligation and fence revocation without erasing attempt history.
Separate execution ownership termination from resource availability and stop acknowledgement.
Expose expiry recovery after current_attempt is cleared; prevent replacement until the approved disposition is committed.
Handle service restart, delayed sweeper, clock discontinuity and concurrent heartbeat/finish according to one serialized policy.
Record the exact reason/deadline/old fence and authorized recovery choices in readback.
checks: A deliberately late timer does not permit writes after the deadline.
Expired work cannot return to ready merely because its current pointer disappeared.
History retains expired attempt, original receipts and recovery decision after replacement.

tasks.title: Implement stop requests and confirmed assignment release
steps: Expose separate stop-requested, stop-observed and assignment-released outcomes where external process state is uncertain.
Authorize safe stop/release under the specific action policy even when a hard hold prevents claim/finish/close.
Perform runtime/process observation outside the write transaction and bind acknowledgements to the expected fence/resource owner.
Release only the requester’s valid ownership or an explicitly authorized operator disposition; preserve holds and operator-only dispatch policy.
Handle timeout, process-tree survival and unknown stop outcomes without declaring resources free.
Make release idempotent and distinguish it from cancellation of work and software release publication.
checks: A blocked task still offers the approved safe stop/recovery path without allowing prohibited forward progress.
An old owner cannot release a replacement’s reservation.
Unconfirmed stop never permits silent reuse of a shared worktree.

tasks.title: Implement failure classification, bounded retry and operator recovery
steps: Classify execution failure as retryable or intervention-required according to pinned policy and retain the original failure evidence.
Create explicit retry decisions with bounded attempts, not-before/backoff and isolation requirements; default to no blind redispatch.
Require safe resource disposition before a retry claim and distinguish retry_wait from blocked/expired recovery.
Implement authorized recovery actions such as confirm stopped, abandon unsafe output, adopt verified context or return to planning.
Record reason, target revision, actor, evidence and audit/readback for operator disposition.
Recheck current holds, dependency outcomes, authority and requirements before any replacement claim.
checks: Retry only becomes eligible after both time and safe-disposition constraints are satisfied.
A retry policy cannot suppress a hard hold or rejected-review obligation.
Failed attempts and every retry/recovery decision remain inspectable.

tasks.title: Reconcile live attempts, jobs and ownership after service restart
steps: Reload authoritative current attempts, deadlines, pending operation/job outcomes and unresolved resource obligations on startup.
Mark uncertain runtime observations unknown until a trusted adapter or operator reconciles them.
Resume timers without resetting claimed_at or granting extra hard budget.
Reject late messages from old service/attempt ownership while preserving legitimate scoped operation readback.
Handle restart during accept, verifier start, stop request, release and expiry disposition.
Expose recovery progress through status/action descriptors rather than silently modifying lifecycle from service code.
checks: Restart never creates a second current execution or resets a hard deadline.
A still-running external worker remains accounted for until safe handoff.
Every recovered state is explainable from durable records and observed runtime evidence.

tasks.title: Run execution races, deadline boundaries and physical-stop validation
steps: Use separate real harness processes and the production service for claim/accept/start/heartbeat/release paths.
Race claim/hold, claim/dependency edits, heartbeat/expiry, finish/expiry and release/replacement with stable operation IDs.
Keep a worker writing in a disposable protected worktree after lease expiry and verify replacement is denied until the approved stop/disposition.
Restart the service and reorder old-fence messages; retain exact source, runtime and clock evidence.
Exercise manual adoption and authorized recovery controls with actual principal/session identities.
Run negative controls proving the harness detects duplicate current ownership and fabricated safe-stop acknowledgements.
checks: No duplicate task/session/resource ownership or post-expiry mutation occurs.
All supported restart and failure cases retain coherent audit/outcome history.
An unexercised platform process-tree cleanup case remains an explicit blocker.

tasks.title: Integrate execution policy with status, actions and service routes
steps: Read each execution/recovery condition through the actual service and compare with mutation authorization at the same relevant revision/time.
Verify next actions and disabled causes are provided by the domain/application contract, including safe recovery under holds.
Remove any lingering current-pointer-only expiry inference or alternate lifecycle rules in supported adapters.
Document command/API behavior for evidence, review and TUI consumers without declaring their future workflows complete.
Run execution plus affected domain/store/service suites on one integrated source identity.
Hand off unresolved findings and exact contracts to the closeout sprint.
checks: Read/action/transaction results agree for active, expired, retrying, released and operator-blocked executions.
Ending an attempt does not erase policy/recovery facts.
Only the independent revalidation gate permits consumers to treat this execution contract as accepted.

tasks.title: Expose profile creation, pinning and requirement validation
steps: Expose accepted profile registry operations with immutable version/content identity and explicit creation authority.
Validate task/container profile selection, required/optional kinds and supported verifier/review/closeout rules.
Pin resolved requirements at work publication and report exact configuration gaps to planning/readiness.
Reject duplicate/conflicting versions and unknown profiles without falling back to focused.
