Handle profile changes on draft/open/active/closed work according to proof-invalidation and expected-revision rules.
Provide migration/repair for candidate empty definitions only when authoritative requirements can be established.
checks: Sibling tasks can use different profiles and preserve them across restart/reopen.
Deleting a required gate/result cannot make claim or close easier.
A profile default edit cannot silently alter active or accepted work.

tasks.title: Capture trustworthy source, configuration and execution input identity
steps: Compute source/configuration identities from actual supported project/worktree inputs, not arbitrary caller strings.
Define tracked/untracked/dirty/generated/excluded file treatment and record verifier executable/config/environment identity.
Bind the snapshot to project, task proof revision, pinned requirements and intended execution/submission subject.
Prevent source changes between capture and verification from producing a falsely current receipt; use immutable inputs or verified before/after binding as approved.
Use cryptographic digest validation and path-safe artifact references with explicit inaccessible/missing-source diagnostics.
Preserve reproducible source context for later review, supersession and backup.
checks: Changing a proof-relevant file or verifier configuration invalidates applicability as specified.
A caller cannot make wrong source current by providing a matching-looking hash string.
Snapshot capture cannot read an unauthorized foreign path through symlink/traversal.

tasks.title: Implement a bounded, attributable real verifier executor

Only a verified actual Git revision is returned as published authority.

tasks.title: Implement reimport, fresh-clone reconciliation and doctor checks
steps: Reimport a named published Git revision into rebuildable local indexes/links while preserving source and author provenance.
Detect divergent manifests, missing artifacts, unsupported memory versions and conflicting local drafts.
Make repeated import idempotent without rewriting historical publication records.
Support fresh-clone initialization of curated memory without importing foreign live work/attempt authority.
Provide read-only doctor diagnostics and explicit reasoned repair plans for broken links/jobs.
Keep project identity and publication trust validation mandatory during clone/rebind/import.
checks: A fresh clone can reconstruct published memory citations at the exact Git revision.
Reimport does not create duplicate entries or silently overwrite local drafts.
Missing/foreign memory artifacts do not become trusted local knowledge.

tasks.title: Implement revision-bound handoff and bounded context bundles
steps: Assemble handoff context from exact work/result/attempt/source/requirement revisions, recent valid evidence and unresolved obligations.
Include resource/ownership safety, what changed, what remains, failed proof and one next permitted action.

Make a no-goal unfamiliar agent able to obtain this context through trusted guide/next routes.
Prevent source text, summaries or arbitrary URLs from overriding trusted action/authority instructions.
checks: A recipient can continue work without chat history and can inspect all referenced proof/context.
A stale handoff is visibly stale and cannot authorize mutation at the old revision.
Context truncation never hides a critical safety or acceptance obligation.

tasks.title: Implement artifact retention roots and safe garbage-collection planning
steps: Enumerate roots from accepted outcomes, failed/historical receipts, live submissions, source versions, published memory, pending jobs and backups.
Implement a read-only retention/GC preview with policy, exact candidates, reachability and required authority.
Preserve mandatory failed/audit provenance and required retained artifact bytes under the approved policy; do not silently prune to meet performance budgets.
Prevent concurrent publication/backup/submission from losing newly referenced artifacts through pinning or transactional root rules.
Make any permitted pruning explicit, reasoned, revision-bound, auditable and recoverable within the chosen retention design.
Keep content hash deduplication scoped so foreign project presence does not grant access.
checks: An artifact referenced by required acceptance/history/memory/backup cannot be silently collected.
A race with new references does not delete live proof.
Previewing retention is read-only; actual pruning requires explicit authorized execution.

tasks.title: Validate source-memory-handoff recovery through the real service
steps: Exercise supported source intake, parser failure, versioned search, citation lookup, draft review/publish, Git crash readback and fresh-clone reconciliation.
Use real files, Git repositories and service operations in disposable projects, not fabricated publication revisions.
Test conflicting human edits, foreign source references, secret redaction, stale context and unsupported memory versions.

Verify failed jobs, drafts and sources remain queryable after recovery.
Record supported-kind coverage and any absent legacy source/memory cases for migration acceptance.
checks: A real source-to-published-memory-to-handoff path is reproducible with valid citations.
Database and Git truth converge after every tested publication interruption.
No source/memory operation leaks project data or bypasses work proof.

tasks.title: Acquire and freeze representative legacy parity inputs
steps: Resolve the baseline external-input register for actual v1 archives/exports/schema versions and retained command behavior.
Hash and preserve read-only representative originals including failures, reviews, force records, reservations, summaries and source/memory links.

checks: Each retained parity assertion has identifiable original evidence.
Absent required legacy inputs are explicit blockers rather than invented representative fixtures.
Raw originals remain unchanged and segregated from execution projects.

tasks.title: Implement dry-run/export/import with complete disposition reports
steps: Implement supported schema detection and deterministic dry-run mapping for every known record family.
Report imported/transformed/quarantined/unsupported/skipped records with raw source ID/hash, reason and target identity.
Export originals and rollback references before irreversible actions; refuse silent overwrite of an existing project.
Bind import to destination project/database identity and approved mapping version.
Preserve malformed/unknown records as retained raw provenance rather than silently dropping them.
Keep import planning read-only until explicit authorized execution.
checks: Every input record has one machine-readable disposition with provenance.
Unknown schema/record types cannot silently disappear.
A dry run performs no canonical mutation and an existing project is not overwritten by default.

tasks.title: Migrate lifecycle, proof and review without converting prose into acceptance
steps: Replace unconditional done/complete/archived-to-Closed normalization with the approved historical-status versus accepted-outcome mapping.
Preserve original lifecycle text, gate requirements, failed receipts, review rejection/approval provenance and force records.
Create accepted v2 outcomes only when the required authoritative legacy evidence and approved mapping actually justify them.
Quarantine ambiguous completion and expose explicit operator reconciliation without fabricating receipts or self-review.
Map timestamps/fences/actor identities carefully and report unsupported clock/authority provenance.
Verify imported complete/verified/cancelled/ambiguous records cannot accidentally unblock default dependencies.
checks: Historical done prose alone cannot become accepted closed.
Failed and rejected evidence remains inspectable after import.
A legacy exception becomes an explicit typed disposition only when its provenance/authority meets the approved mapping.

tasks.title: Migrate hierarchy, cycles, assignments and dependency history
steps: Map fixed-tree sprint records into one canonical cycle/assignment identity with preserved legacy-ID lookup.
Retain task decomposition, cross-sprint edges, cancelled/deferred commitments and carry-over provenance where evidence exists.
Detect invalid parents, cycles, duplicate IDs/live assignments and cross-project references before committing.
Bind dependency satisfaction to approved accepted outcomes from the lifecycle mapping, not legacy label shortcuts.
Record unsupported or ambiguous container semantics explicitly rather than fabricating clean rollups.
Provide deterministic reimport behavior and conflict handling for partially imported mappings.
checks: Legacy sprint compatibility does not create duplicate writable sprint/cycle records.
No imported edge is silently removed merely because its endpoint is corrupt.
Repeated import preserves identities and does not duplicate assignments or accepted history.

tasks.title: Materialize legacy source/memory and interruption-safe import
steps: Materialize supported raw source bytes, citations, memory publication Git references and operational links under the destination project boundary.
Preserve missing/external artifact diagnostics and original reference hashes instead of inventing local content.
Use staged idempotent import jobs for filesystem/Git effects and transactionally commit canonical mappings.
Recover interruption between artifact copy, database mapping and memory reconciliation using readback/manifests.

Verify resumed import cannot link to foreign project artifacts or overwrite unrelated human memory edits.
checks: A successful record-count import cannot hide missing required source/memory materialization.
Crash/resume produces one target mapping per original identity.
All preserved citations either resolve to actual bytes/revisions or report an explicit migration limitation.

tasks.title: Implement consistent online backup with a full project manifest
steps: Use the supported consistent SQLite backup mechanism through the selected project authority, not a casual copy of a live main database file.
Bind backup to database/schema/project revision, referenced blobs/source versions, pending jobs and published memory Git revision.
Pin artifact roots while copying and verify hashes/manifest completeness before marking a backup complete.
Record credentials/secrets handling, permissions and encryption policy if approved; never expose secrets in the manifest.
Write into a new destination with explicit overwrite protection and interruption recovery.
Validate backups during concurrent permitted writers and prove the captured graph is self-consistent.
checks: A backup contains a coherent database plus every required referenced artifact/memory revision or fails explicitly.
An interrupted backup is not advertised as restorable complete.
Backup cannot overwrite an existing target or read a foreign project without explicit authority.

tasks.title: Implement safe restore, restore epochs and service reconciliation
steps: Validate backup manifest, schema/runtime compatibility, project identity and artifact hashes before activation.
Require exclusive maintenance ownership and explicit destination/overwrite confirmation.
Assign the approved restored database epoch/rebind state so pre-restore credentials/operations/fences cannot silently regain authority.
Restore referenced blobs and named memory revision consistently, preserving conflicting human files through explicit disposition.

checks: Old pending operation IDs and executor fences cannot mutate the restored project.
A corrupt or incomplete backup is rejected before replacing live state.
Restore followed by service start yields explicit recovery obligations and valid history, not blindly resumed workers.

tasks.title: Implement read-only doctor and explicit revision-bound repair
steps: Inspect identity, schema, requirement declarations, parents/edges, attempts/resources, operation/jobs, artifacts/indexes and memory reconciliation safely.
Distinguish canonical corruption, stale derived state, unavailable artifact and unsupported runtime with precise scope.
Generate a reasoned repair preview naming exact target revision, changes, preserved history, risks and required authority.
Implement only approved deterministic repairs through the canonical executor/maintenance boundary; never synthesize accepted proof or replacement work.
Preserve a before-repair snapshot/backup and durable audit/readback.
Require revalidation of affected invariants and expose unresolved/manual-only repairs explicitly.
checks: Doctor inspection is read-only and cannot claim it repaired anything.
A stale repair preview or insufficient authority is rejected.
Repair never deletes failed history, invents a passing receipt or normalizes a corrupt identity into trusted data.

tasks.title: Expose migration/backup/restore/doctor service and maintenance routes
steps: Expose dry-run/import/export/backup/restore/doctor/repair through supported application routes and explicit maintenance mode where required.
Validate project/destination identity, authority, reason, expected revision and confirmation scope.
Return durable job/operation IDs, stage, exact artifact manifests and readback guidance for long/uncertain operations.

Integrate registry entries only for complete supported operations.
checks: A user can perform safe maintenance without manually editing SQLite.
Unavailable/corrupt/unsupported outcomes are actionable and distinct.
All external side effects are traceable to one authorized operation/job identity.

tasks.title: Run real migration, backup/restore and repair acceptance

Inject failures between import/backup/restore/repair stages and observe supported recovery/readback.
Test fresh/upgrade/reopen compatibility and reject unsupported runtime/schema combinations.
Record missing legacy/platform inputs as blocked evidence and retain complete originals/failure transcripts.

Full project backup/restore is proven beyond the SQLite rows alone.
No migration/repair step fabricates acceptance or loses historical provenance.

tasks.title: Reconcile the public command registry and compatibility aliases
steps: Map every retained v1/M02 public command and alias to an accepted application use case or explicit approved limitation.
Inventory actual existing update/upgrade, status/prime, work, sprint, evidence, review, memory and doctor routes before editing.

Integrate registry changes as one shared-file owner and publish an exhaustive route/acceptance map.

No registry entry falsely advertises a stub or unaccepted feature.
Aliases cannot bypass auth, lifecycle or project selection.

tasks.title: Implement project, identity and actor/session public commands
steps: Expose explicit init/info/select/rebind and supported authority/session operations through the canonical application/service boundary.
Keep default project resolution local and return precise missing/stale/foreign metadata guidance.
Validate mutually exclusive/repeated options before invoking a mutation, without adding policy bypass flags.

checks: A fresh user can initialize the intended directory without seeing another project’s data.
Actor/role text in CLI flags cannot self-authorize privileged enrollment.
Machine and human outcomes describe the same actual committed result.

tasks.title: Implement milestone, sprint/cycle and work planning commands
steps: Expose milestone/task create/edit/publish/archive, cycle/sprint create/activate/current/status/board/report/close and assignment/carry-over operations.
Expose profile/version/gate selection, dates, dispatch policy and dependency edits using accepted structured inputs.
Preserve compatibility spellings without duplicated models or SQL access.

Return exact rollups, readiness gaps, assignment history and safe next actions from service DTOs.
Cover malformed input, invalid parent/cycle/profile and stale planning confirmation.
checks: The full two-cycle/four-task plan can be created and inspected from the public CLI.
Different sibling profiles and cross-cycle prerequisites are visible and enforced.
CLI cannot make a cycle active or closed by writing a display-status field.

tasks.title: Implement work queues, attention, status and history commands
steps: Expose list/show/next/ready/parallel/review-candidates, current attempts, recovery/operator inboxes and history/diagnostics.

Terminal output does not mistake capped rows for full project totals.
Unknown/corrupt/unavailable states are visible without inventing normal work states.

tasks.title: Implement consolidated agent execution and finish/release commands
steps: Expose guide/start/claim/accept/resume/checkpoint/heartbeat/finish and stop/release/adopt paths through the accepted executor.

Reject stale/foreign sessions, active holds, wrong fences and invalid argument combinations consistently.
checks: An agent can follow the complete supported claim-to-finish or safe-release loop from CLI responses.
Timeout does not lead to a new automatic operation ID and duplicate finish.
No accepted/closed wording appears when only a submission or pending close intent exists.

tasks.title: Implement evidence, review and explicit operator commands
steps: Expose declared verification execution, receipt/gate inspection, review open/show/approve/reject/return/revoke and closeout inspection.

Return denied authority, stale proof/revision, pending external work and exact operation readback explicitly.
Validate argument parsing without reconstructing independent-review or lifecycle rules in the CLI.
checks: All operator decisions are possible without manual database edits and are auditable.
A plain agent cannot force a gate, waive an edge or approve its own required review.
A returned/rejected review is not printed as missing/awaiting ordinary review.

tasks.title: Implement source, memory, handoff and maintenance commands
steps: Expose supported source add/inspect/search/citation, memory draft/publish/reconcile and revision-bound handoff/context operations.
Expose import/export dry-run/dispositions, backup/restore, doctor and explicit repair through supported maintenance boundaries.
Show actual source/Git/backup identities and pending/failed job stages without guessing success.
Validate sensitive paths/project identity and protect secrets in output and process arguments.
Keep published memory distinct from drafts and canonical work authority.
Cover interrupted operations and foreign/unsupported source/backup/schema outcomes.

Git publication reports the actual verified commit, not an intended one.
Dry-run/doctor remain read-only and explicit repair requires authorized current context.

tasks.title: Standardize machine envelopes, exit codes, help and operation readback

A structured response never contains a misleading success flag on a rejected or pending mutation.
Help examples and registry schemas are executable and agree on accepted flags.

Run overlapping project IDs, foreign selectors, stale sessions and interrupted request cases.

Aliases preserve semantics and cannot provide a bypass.
No fake service controller or fabricated passing receipt closes a CLI parity row.

Document operation/action semantics and source files for downstream consumers without requiring private chat context.
Run all affected CLI/protocol/application suites on the combined source and retain failures.
Hand off a read-only source/evidence packet to independent public-contract review.
checks: Workflow/TUI owners have actual registered routes and exact schemas, not proposed spellings.
Known unavailable features remain visibly unavailable and mapped to approved scope.
The public contract is accepted only after independent review and exact-tree revalidation.

steps: Expose workflow list/show/resolve for the approved core package through the Rust application and public discovery routes.
Validate workflow, directive, protocol and command registry identities and dependencies before returning an executable action.
Reject unknown/missing/incompatible assets with typed actionable errors.

Preserve core route/context/plan/claim/finish/review/audit/handoff/health/memory workflows.
Keep asset registration and manifest changes serialized through the steward.

An asset referencing an unavailable or wrong-version command fails validation.
Workflow discovery never mutates work or fabricates a ready task.

steps: Build guide/next from one revisioned canonical snapshot plus server-owned allowed/denied actions and trusted registry version.
Return current subject, requirements, evidence/recovery gaps, one selected safe action and refresh time/event.
Represent no-goal, empty queue, ordinary queued, policy-paused, unavailable and operator-intervention outcomes distinctly.
Bound payloads and context/history lookups while preserving every critical safety/acceptance reason.
Do not infer close/claim eligibility from labels or produce a separate persisted workflow lifecycle.
Invalidate stale action context and route unknown operation outcomes to readback before retry.
checks: Guidance and service action descriptors agree for every status/actor condition.
A no-goal empty project does not cause guidance to invent work.
Large history does not make routine guide calls load all attempts or memory.

tasks.title: Implement trusted structured argv and instruction/data separation
steps: Compile executable actions from trusted registry templates using typed IDs, exact argv, cwd, shell=false, revision/fence and operation identity.
Treat task descriptions, source text, memory citations and declared verifier text as untrusted display data.

Validate argument size, escaping, path scope and supported runner identity.
Reject missing required/blocking directives and incompatible action versions rather than issuing a convenient fallback.
Add adversarial content cases with instructions to ignore gates, switch projects or execute shell metacharacters.

A workflow cannot authorize a command the application would deny.
All executable actions carry sufficient current identity for transactional validation.

tasks.title: Connect plan/claim/resume/checkpoint/evidence/finish workflows
steps: Update core workflow assets to the actual public registry, cycle model, acceptance profiles and execution/submission contract.
Provide plan validation/launch, actor-aware claim/start/resume, checkpoint, genuine verification and consolidated finish/close guidance.
Retain conditional no-goal behavior and normal focused-profile completion without fabricated review.
Offer safe release/recovery when execution cannot proceed, without deleting holds or expired obligations.
Return context/actions after useful transitions to reduce unnecessary repeated status calls.
Keep all transitions in application/store even when workflow prose describes the intended sequence.
checks: An unfamiliar agent can execute the normal happy path from returned guidance without a bespoke task prompt.
Required proof cannot be skipped through an asset or alias.
Guidance never calls complete a closed accepted result.

tasks.title: Connect independent review, operator recovery and failure workflows
steps: Guide authorized independent reviewers to exact immutable submissions and all current/failed evidence.
Distinguish reject/return/reconcile, expiry recovery, failed execution, pause and hard-hold resolution.
Offer typed exception/waiver actions only to authorized operators with required reason/comment/revision/scope context.
Route stale fences, restored epochs and unknown operation outcomes to safe readback/recovery rather than retry loops.
Explain physical-stop/resource disposition before replacement work.
Preserve all failed receipts/reviews/attempts and reference them in remediation guidance.
checks: Expiry is not presented as an ordinary review-approve action.
A plain agent never receives an executable operator override as an allowed action.
Recovery guidance cannot clear an obligation without the authoritative operation.

tasks.title: Connect cited context, memory and handoff workflows
steps: Use the accepted context/handoff service to include revision-bound work, source, requirements, proof and unresolved resource state.
Cite curated memory by actual Git revision and distinguish drafts/operational notes.
Offer source retrieval/publication/reconciliation only through permitted public routes.
Make truncation, stale citations, missing artifacts and index lag explicit.

checks: Handoff references resolve to actual preserved source/proof/memory identities.
A stale or foreign memory item cannot silently steer a protected action.
The successor can find the next safe action without relying on hidden chat context.

tasks.title: Validate unfamiliar-agent workflows across two actual harnesses
steps: Run scripted conformance and actual model-operated no-goal sessions through at least two supported harness entry points using the production service.
Give only the project entry/discovery instruction, not a bespoke implementation prompt or fake desired results.
Exercise normal completion, queued/paused/operator-only, failed/stale proof, rejected review, expired/replaced session and unknown-outcome recovery.
Use real verifier execution and genuinely distinct reviewer principals where configured.
Measure calls per useful transition, unchanged reads, payload bytes and verification-to-close time under the preapproved workload including long history.
Record harness/operator identity and unavailable capability as a blocker; a scripted loop alone is not model-operated evidence.
checks: Two actual harness paths complete or safely release/recover using returned trusted context.
No fabricated proof, hidden parent prompt or direct database manipulation is needed.
All measurements and transcripts are tied to exact source/registry/runtime identities.

tasks.title: Validate workflow package identity and close parity gaps
steps: Reconcile packaged skills, source workflow assets, directive registry, public command map and actual no-goal transcripts.
Remove stale route spellings and update version identities through serialized manifest ownership.
Record every retained v1 guidance behavior as observed/unsupported with explicit approved disposition.
Test unknown package version, missing asset and mismatched installed identity fail closed.
Run asset validators and the actual no-goal suite on the integrated tree.
Provide the release steward a complete required workflow/TUI/share asset manifest.

Core guidance is not marked deferred because CRUD commands work.
No historical failure or unsupported harness is relabeled as passing parity.

tasks.title: Replace client-derived action policy with service descriptors

A blocked task can show an authorized safe stop action returned by the service.
Contradictory or unsupported DTOs cannot trigger a mutation.

Reconnect via snapshot resync after cursor gaps and resolve unknown outcomes before retry.
checks: A late Project A response cannot repaint or mutate Project B.
Service outage never shows fabricated fresh counts or switches to a global project.
An uncertain mutation remains visible and is resolved by original operation ID.

tasks.title: Implement overview, exact attention totals and stable navigation
steps: Build overview around exact server totals, active cycles and separate review/recovery/operator attention summaries.
Keep project identity, freshness and primary safety notices visible before decorative branding.
Implement stable-ID selection, back stack, direct ID navigation, filters and a searchable action palette.

checks: Selection remains on the same entity after rows reorder or new work arrives.
Exact totals come from the service, not the number of rendered rows.
Keyboard navigation works without color or a mouse and exposes an obvious exit.

tasks.title: Implement milestone/cycle planning, readiness and scope views
steps: Render milestone outcomes, cycle commitments, task assignments and cross-cycle prerequisites using server projections.
Show accepted work versus reconciled scope separately and explain deferred/cancelled/replaced assignments.

checks: Users can plan and launch the supported two-cycle example through real service actions.
A stale scope preview cannot activate/close a changed cycle.
Carry-over history is visible without losing task identity or overstating completed work.

steps: Show primary explanation, all secondary reasons, prerequisites, pinned requirements, execution/submission context and next permitted actions.

Show raw failed proof plus explicit exception rather than painting forced acceptance as an ordinary pass.

Use advanced diagnostics for fences/enum/schema details while keeping ordinary workflow language understandable.

A reviewer cannot accidentally approve a different/newer submission after refresh.
All required reasons remain accessible at every supported terminal geometry.

steps: Support UTF-8/grapheme-aware editing, bracketed paste, multiline structured inputs, validation errors and recoverable drafts.

Keep parser/input validation local while all business permission and lifecycle checks remain service-owned.

Resize or stale refresh cannot turn a dismissed dialog into a mutation.
A malformed form preserves editable input and returns a clear typed correction path.

steps: Provide separate queues/details for expiry recovery, rejected-review reconciliation, runtime failure, policy hold and corruption.

tasks.title: Implement memory/context/history and maintenance navigation
steps: Expose cited source/context, published memory versus drafts and revision-bound handoff from supported service DTOs.
Allow safe navigation into operation/audit/receipt/review history with bounded pages and clear current/historical distinction.
Display actual Git/source/artifact identity, missing citations and index lag without inventing source excerpts.
Expose backup/import/doctor/repair status and navigation to supported commands where full in-terminal forms are not accepted scope.
Keep secrets/redacted content protected and sanitize external text.
Do not introduce a local memory database or bypass publisher/maintenance authority.
checks: A citation opens the exact preserved version or an explicit unavailable diagnostic.
Historical failures remain accessible without overwhelming the default view.
Maintenance affordances cannot silently mutate or invoke an unregistered shell command.

tasks.title: Complete independent width/height breakpoints and accessible fallback
steps: Retain multi-pane wide layouts, use focused list/detail on medium sizes, and reduce chrome to single-pane/scrolling content in short editor panels.
Treat width and height independently; never show only a resize wall where basic navigation/read access can fit.
Test at minimum 144x40, 100x32, 80x24, 80x12, 60x10, 44x12, 36x8 and 24x6, plus live resize and invalid geometry events.
Preserve target/impact/exit visibility and disable consequential confirmation when it cannot be read safely.
Support plain-text/no-color behavior, readable focus, reduced motion and correct wide/combining Unicode cell measurement.
Keep tiny-terminal fallback honest about any safe interaction limit rather than silently truncating a critical reason.
checks: The dashboard remains navigable in a short editor terminal without requiring 48x18 minimum size.
A tiny terminal can inspect/exit safely but cannot confirm an unreadable destructive action.
Resize preserves selection, draft form data and pending-operation identity.

tasks.title: Run mounted real-service terminal workflow and outage tests
steps: Launch the compiled TUI in real PTYs against the actual Rust service, not fake dashboard/controller data.
Perform plan/claim/verify/review/finish/release/recovery and project switch actions with genuine evidence and registered identities.
Exercise all listed dimensions, live resize, UTF-8 paste, multiline input, cancellation and terminal restoration.
Interrupt service before/after commit and verify stale view, original operation readback and no unintended retries.
Inject scoped corruption through an owned negative-test setup and verify valid siblings/disabled action explanations.
Retain PTY transcripts/screenshots as observations with raw service requests/outcomes; presentation fixtures remain supplementary.
checks: A mounted TUI action completes the same canonical operation as CLI/service with correct audit/readback.
No fixture-side DTO normalization is used to hide a real protocol mismatch.
All supported geometry/outage/input cases preserve safety and usable recovery.

tasks.title: Integrate UX language, client boundaries and installed asset contract
steps: Audit TypeScript for direct SQLite access, repeated CLI-spawn refreshes and independent status/action/lifecycle policy.
Review all normal-screen language for internal enum, raw SQL, fence/schema/module and debug-message leakage.
Reconcile real-service PTY findings with focused presentation tests and retain failed runs.
Provide release packaging a full source/dist/installer asset inventory and actual runtime compatibility requirements.
Run typecheck, tests, installer identity and real-service UX acceptance on the integrated source.
Document genuine accessible/small-terminal limits and unresolved unsupported environments without calling them passed.
checks: The TUI is demonstrably a service client with only ephemeral presentation/pending-request state.
Normal status language preserves the product distinctions and exposes advanced details on demand.
The release handoff includes the complete TUI tree rather than only one entrypoint.

tasks.title: Freeze the integrated scenario graph and evidence harness
steps: Freeze one clean integrated source and absolute production binary/TUI/contract identities for this acceptance run.
Map every final-form requirement and original M02 acceptance row to named positive, negative, boundary, race and restart scenarios.
Use disposable projects with real service operation setup and genuine verifier/reviewer identities.
Define separate artifact paths per scenario and strict exit handling; skipped required cases remain failures/blockers.
Restrict direct database corruption to named negative-test setup and preserve before/after state; never insert successful receipts/outcomes.
Self-test the runner with deliberately wrong result, missing receipt and child nonzero exit.
checks: The runner fails if any required scenario is missing, skipped, mismatched-source or falsely successful.
Every scenario has a reproducible command and exact expected invariant, not just a screenshot.
Only one source identity is called the integrated acceptance candidate.

tasks.title: Prove project init to parallel plan to accepted closeout
steps: Initialize a fresh project and create a milestone, two parallel cycles and at least four dependent tasks with different valid profiles.
Validate and activate the plan while normal prerequisites remain queued.
Use multiple real agent sessions to claim/start/checkpoint/run real proof/finish; use a distinct reviewer where configured.
Show complete does not unblock a default edge, then accepted closed does; reconcile cycle scope and milestone closeout.
Carry one incomplete task forward and verify identity/history and accepted-versus-reconciled counts.
Read all outcomes through CLI JSON, service and mounted TUI at recorded revisions.
checks: The entire supported product loop is achieved without direct success-state insertion.
Parallel tasks and cross-cycle prerequisites behave exactly as the final contract.
Final container acceptance references exact accepted/disposed scope and genuine proof.

tasks.title: Prove every status, secondary reason and action combination
steps: Construct every required task state through supported operations, including queued, paused, retry, schedule if approved, failed/missing/stale proof, awaiting/rejected review, complete, closed, expired and operator hold.
Combine pause/dependency, expiry/hold, failed proof/review and multiple prerequisites to verify primary precedence and retained subjects.
Compare actor-specific action descriptors across agent/reviewer/operator for the same canonical facts.
Exercise corrupted/unavailable/incompatible axes separately from product status.
Attempt each representative denied transition through service and alternate supported adapters.
Record exact as_of/revision so real time progression is not misreported as disagreement.
checks: No requested meaning is collapsed into one label or generic failure.
All applicable reasons are preserved and action denials match transaction outcomes.
Due/overdue and service availability do not masquerade as execution expiry.

tasks.title: Prove multi-agent planning/execution/acceptance race safety
steps: Race claims, holds, dependency edits, cycle assignments, scope changes, source edits, reviews and final close across separate processes.
Include stale entity revision, stale proof revision, stale fence and restored-database epoch cases independently.
Assert one current task/session/resource execution and one valid accepted outcome under competing mutations.
Verify accepted/rejected operations and audit counts agree with one legal serialized order.
Use real verified submissions for acceptance races; do not bypass proof to speed the test.
Retain seeds, process timelines and minimal counterexamples for failures.
checks: No race permits duplicate ownership, missing audit, unauthorized close or cross-project reference.
The same operation ID does not create duplicate semantic effects.
Performance measurements do not substitute for invariant assertions.

tasks.title: Prove unknown outcomes and partial external-operation recovery
steps: Interrupt before admission, during queueing, after canonical commit-before-response and after external effect-before-recorded acknowledgement.
Cover verifier artifact creation, submission/close, Git publication, backup and permitted maintenance jobs.
Resolve by original scoped operation/job identity and validate definitive not-found/expired-admission semantics.
Replay exact and changed payloads and test late arrival after an operation is conclusively rejected.
Verify TUI/CLI stale views and pending journals never invent success or retry with a new ID.
Inspect retained failure history, resource obligations and audit/readback after restart.
checks: Every tested uncertain outcome converges to one durable result or remains explicitly unresolved with a safe action.
No duplicate publication/summary/close/claim is created by recovery.
Clients do not classify a timeout as certain mutation failure.

tasks.title: Prove isolation across every public and cached surface
steps: Create two projects with overlapping work/actor/session/source/operation IDs and identical artifact hashes where allowed.
Probe implicit/explicit selection, parent/dependency references, proof, memory, search, diagnostics, backup and operation readback.
Exercise copied metadata, symlink/traversal, stale socket/database epoch and project move/rebind.
Switch the mounted TUI during slow requests and force late responses from the old project.
Verify cached counts, snippets, action contexts and pending journals remain correctly scoped.
Test authorized explicit import only under its approved mapping and preserve provenance.
checks: No surface leaks another project’s content or mutates its records.
A stale/foreign identity never falls back silently to a global project.
Identical local IDs/content hashes do not bypass access scope.

tasks.title: Prove migration, corrupted-record recovery and full restore integration
steps: Import the accepted representative legacy inputs into a fresh destination and execute retained supported workflows against migrated work.
Verify historical complete labels, failed reviews and force records retain approved dispositions and do not fabricate accepted closure.
Introduce scoped corruption to parents/requirements/attempt clocks/receipts and verify safe valid-sibling behavior and explicit repair.
Back up the real project including source/blobs/published memory, restore and verify hashes/revisions/citations.
Test old pending operations/fences after restore and confirm they cannot regain authority.
Retain source-to-target disposition reports and before/after diagnostic/readback evidence.
checks: Legacy parity is proven from actual originals and all required provenance survives.
A restored project is self-consistent and safe before new execution.
No repair or migration silently normalizes corruption into successful work.

tasks.title: Prove no-goal agent and mounted-terminal cross-surface workflows
steps: Have an unfamiliar actual harness obtain guide/next, execute genuine work and hand off to another principal through cited service context.
Have a human/reviewer use mounted TUI screens to inspect failed/current proof and make the required decision.
Run short-terminal, resize, paste/cancel and service-unavailable cases during real pending operations.
Compare selected project, snapshot, status, actions and operation outcomes across the harness, CLI and TUI.
Measure context/call efficiency under the accepted budget without hiding missing obligations.
Record harness identity and real PTY/service transcripts; scripted-only or fake-controller cases remain supplementary.
checks: The product works without private chat context or a bespoke parent implementation prompt.
Human and agent surfaces cannot disagree about acceptance authority at the same snapshot.
No UI interaction during failure issues an unintended mutation.

tasks.title: Reconcile all integration evidence and original acceptance obligations
steps: Index every scenario by exact source/build/environment, inputs, operations, assertions, outcome and artifact hashes.
Map all 48 original M02 obligations and final-form requirements to actual observed evidence, keeping historical task status separate.
Identify any skipped/unsupported/faked/normalized or mismatched-source result and mark the corresponding gate blocked.
Record findings with severity, reproducer, owner, fix boundary and required reruns.
Reject claims based solely on test counts, source ZIP integrity or prior candidate reports.
Produce the independent integration-review packet without certifying release/package/platform readiness.
checks: Every required row has genuine current-tree evidence or an explicit blocker.
No fixture normalization masks an unresolved service/protocol bug.
The ledger cannot be made green by dropping a failed required scenario.

tasks.title: Audit authority, project paths and untrusted input boundaries
steps: Independently test credential/role/session/delegation/review boundaries and alternate lower-level public routes.
Probe symlink/check-open races, precreated sockets, foreign metadata/artifacts, terminal control sequences and source-to-command injection.
Fuzz bounded request/DTO/receipt/profile parsing with retained minimal failing inputs.
Test rate/size limits and redaction so invalid requests cannot amplify unauthenticated audit storage or leak secrets.
Verify maintenance/restore/update paths retain the same selected-project authority and exclusive access guarantees.
State the local OS threat-model limits and record unsupported platform checks as blockers.
checks: No authorized boundary can be crossed by forged role/ID, path escape or untrusted command text.
Malformed input is bounded and produces typed errors without panic or secret leakage.
The report names exact tested binaries, scopes and unresolved residual risks.

tasks.title: Run process, disk, clock and service failure-boundary tests
steps: Inject process kill, service restart, child survival, disk full, permission failure, artifact loss and interrupted write/job stages in owned disposable projects.
Exercise exact/late deadlines, approved wall-clock discontinuity behavior and reordered old-fence messages.
Test failure during migration, backup, restore, profile publication and accepted close bookkeeping.
Assert database integrity, one current ownership, durable audit/outcome and visible unresolved recovery.
Capture filesystem/runtime details and do not claim literal power-loss testing from a process-kill simulation.
Preserve failed evidence and all reproducer scripts.
checks: No tested failure produces accepted partial state, lost required audit or blind redispatch.
Late/old executors remain fenced and physical resources remain protected.
Untested power/filesystem/platform boundaries are explicitly qualified, not generalized away.

tasks.title: Measure real multi-agent load and identify bounded hot paths
steps: Run the approved workload mix of claims, heartbeats, evidence, reviews, planning edits, status pages, search and TUI subscriptions against the native service.
Use preapproved work/history/agent counts and record hardware/toolchain/SQLite/build identities.
Measure queue wait, writer hold, read latency, response bytes, memory, WAL growth/checkpointing and heartbeat fairness separately.
Assert correctness while measuring throughput; do not benchmark a no-op fake service.
Identify history-sized scans, lock contention and projection/index lag with query/trace evidence.
Publish failing budgets and candidate optimization boundaries without changing policy or thresholds.
checks: Every claimed performance result includes its workload and environment.
The benchmark continuously checks ownership/audit/status invariants, not just request rate.
Threshold failures remain visible and drive bounded fixes.

tasks.title: Optimize measured hot paths without duplicating policy
steps: Use the measured profile to choose bounded set-based/current-context reads, indexes or cache changes, not speculative rewrites.
Preserve one canonical evaluator and final transactional authorization; never restore a faster divergent SQL eligibility predicate.
Bound historical decoding, avoid N+1 relations and shorten write transactions while keeping snapshot consistency.
Improve fairness/coalescing only within accepted heartbeat/operation semantics.
Compare optimized outputs with the canonical oracle across normal/corrupt/racing snapshots.
Rerun the identical load workload and report before/after metrics with unchanged budgets.
checks: Optimization preserves status/action/proof/rollup equivalence and isolation.
The agreed load budgets pass on the measured supported environment or remain a blocker.
No performance gain is achieved by dropping secondary reasons, exact totals or audit history.

tasks.title: Run sustained soak, leak and recovery-convergence checks
steps: Run the preapproved duration/workload with repeated claims/reviews/retries, UI reconnects, source indexing, memory publication and backup jobs.
Track memory/file descriptors/process descendants/disk/WAL/job backlog over time.
Inject bounded restarts and recoverable failures during the soak and verify convergence without lost operations or leaked reservations.
Validate retained history and pending-job cleanup without pruning required proof to meet resource budgets.
Stop safely on invariant failure and retain the final database/artifact snapshots for diagnosis.
Rerun after repairs on exact integrated source rather than resuming a failed run and calling it passed.
checks: No unbounded leak/backlog or unresolved ownership accumulates under the accepted workload.
Recovery converges within approved budgets with history intact.
Duration/environment limitations are explicit and cannot be reported as a completed soak.

tasks.title: Audit dependencies, executor trust and release security policy
steps: Inventory exact Rust/npm/build-script/compiler/installer dependencies and license/security obligations from lockfiles and actual build inputs.
Verify current relevant advisories and supported runtime requirements against official primary sources at execution time; record retrieval dates and decisions.
Audit verifier attestation, artifact digests, release signature/checksum origin and secret handling in CI/publication.
Pin or explicitly justify floating build inputs and ensure updates trigger compatible revalidation.
Check test-only fault controls cannot be enabled through production unauthenticated requests.
Record remediation or approved noncritical risk disposition without claiming a dependency scanner proves the whole product secure.
checks: No unresolved release-blocking dependency/runtime/trust issue remains.
Production builds exclude unauthenticated test failpoints and secret material.
All current external verification is dated and bound to actual dependency/artifact identities.

tasks.title: Qualify compatibility, backup concurrency and restoration recovery
steps: Run the approved schema/API/status/workflow/client compatibility matrix on supported native binaries.
Test old client/new service, new client/old service, incompatible assets and partial installed-version combinations.
Back up under concurrent writers/jobs and restore with artifact/memory references verified.
Attempt stale pre-restore operation/fence/cursor reuse and verify epoch scoping.
Test rollback only across explicitly compatible schema boundaries and prove incompatible downgrade refusal.
Retain per-combination observed pass/unsupported/failure results.
checks: Supported combinations preserve semantics and unsupported combinations fail clearly.
Concurrent backup captures a self-consistent recoverable project.
Rollback cannot silently reopen an incompatible database with an old binary.

tasks.title: Harden strict validation aggregation and evidence authenticity
steps: Integrate all required real-service, security, fault, migration, no-goal, PTY and load gates with explicit evidence classes and strict required-case handling.
Fail on child command errors, missing results, skipped required platforms, wrong-source evidence or incomplete scenario coverage.
Verify source/binary/contract/artifact hashes and prevent old logs from being reused for a changed candidate.
Retain failures and rerun lineage instead of overwriting one latest-success file.
Add tampered-result, zero-tests, timeout and fake-fixture-only canary tests for the aggregator.
Keep artifact/plan/source integrity checks distinct from product correctness and release acceptance.
checks: The aggregate cannot report success when a required child failed, skipped or did not run.
Tampered or stale evidence is rejected.
A valid full pass names exactly which source/build/platform/scenario set was exercised.

tasks.title: Rerun integrated hardening and resolve the release-blocker ledger
steps: Integrate bounded repairs through their owners and rerun all affected tests on one combined clean source identity.
Reconcile invariant, security, performance, migration and no-goal findings with exact evidence and dispositions.
Require closure of all must-have/integrity/isolation/authority/proof blockers; approved optional deferrals need owners and visible limits.
Verify the original M02 and final-form acceptance matrices remain fully covered after optimizations.
Publish native-platform gaps and required release qualification checks as explicit remaining work.
Hand a reproducible hardening packet to the independent review/reconciliation/revalidation chain.
checks: No unresolved must-have blocker is hidden by an optional-deferral label.
The same combined tree passes correctness and approved load/fault/security budgets.
This gate does not claim publication or installed-platform release proof that belongs to later sprints.

tasks.title: Freeze package contents, provenance and supported runtime policy
steps: Define required bin/bwrk, complete TUI distribution, wizard, workflow/skill/spec/share assets and metadata for every supported target.
Bind binary/TUI/schema/API/status/workflow/memory/toolchain identities to one source commit/tree and artifact manifest.
Enforce the approved actual linked SQLite/runtime features and supported Node/compiler policy on each release target.
Distinguish source archive, built candidate package, installed prefix and published artifact identities.
Specify reproducibility expectations, signature/checksum origin and immutable artifact naming.
Reject mixed-source, stale-binary or missing-required-asset packages before staging.
checks: A package cannot omit a required TUI/workflow/wizard file or combine mismatched contract identities.
The linked runtime floor/features are checked on the actual built binary.
Manifest provenance identifies exact source bytes rather than just a semantic version string.

tasks.title: Implement clean deterministic release build and asset verification
steps: Build Rust and the full TypeScript TUI from a clean accepted source checkout with pinned/recorded toolchains.
Include canonical workflow/skill/schema assets and verify their manifest identity against the compiled binary.
Refuse skip-build/stale-dist shortcuts in release acceptance unless matching source/build identity is cryptographically established.
Generate platform archive manifests and checksums deterministically where supported; document unavoidable nondeterminism.
Validate archive extraction paths, permissions, executable bits, symlink policy and no secret/cache inclusion.
Rebuild in an isolated checkout to verify the agreed reproducibility contract.
checks: A stale globally installed binary or old dist directory cannot enter an accepted package unnoticed.
Clean extraction contains all required paths and verified bytes.
Every build command/output/runtime identity is retained; build failure cannot produce a successful release manifest.

tasks.title: Complete multi-screen installer workflow and responsive interaction
steps: Preserve the canonical wizard source/bundle/embedded generation path and existing responsive design foundations.
Implement clear multi-screen selection/review/install/result stages with supported multi-select choices and explicit installation scope.
Show selected prefix, components, version/source, runtime prerequisites, PATH/shell-profile effects and cancellation behavior before changes.
Adapt short/narrow terminals with scrolling/single-pane layouts rather than an unusable minimum-size wall.
Keep no-shell-profile-mutation as a supported path and make any environment changes opt-in and reversible.
Test installer cancellation/resume/failed validation separately from actual package installation proof.
checks: User can inspect and confirm exactly what will be installed and where at small terminal sizes.
Cancelling before commit leaves the existing install and shell configuration unchanged.
Generated wizard and embedded payload match canonical source bytes.

tasks.title: Implement safe archive verification and atomic prefix activation
steps: Verify artifact origin/signature/checksum and required manifest before extracting executable content.
Reject traversal, malicious symlinks, wrong target/ABI, unsupported runtime and mixed asset identities.
Stage a complete versioned prefix and atomically activate the executable/TUI/share set under an installation lock.
Preserve the prior complete set until activation and post-install identity checks succeed; restore it on supported failure.
Avoid privilege escalation and implicit shell-profile edits; honor explicit user-selected prefix safely.
Protect live project databases and never run a schema migration merely as an unreviewed side effect of copying a binary.
checks: Interrupted installation yields the old complete set or the new complete set, never mixed assets.
Malformed/untrusted archives are rejected before unsafe extraction or execution.
A disposable-prefix installation works without modifying shell profiles or project data.

tasks.title: Complete update/upgrade readback and active-service coordination
steps: Retain existing update/upgrade entry points but replace inferred version-from-output with actual installed binary/assets manifest verification.
Bind update requests to a selected release identity and recorded operation/job stage.
Coordinate active service compatibility, pending work and restart/drain policy without terminating unsafe executions blindly.
Keep binary activation separate from explicit database/schema migration with backup/compatibility preconditions.
Recover interruption before/after activation and report exact installed/previous versions and rollback eligibility.
Reject unsupported downgrade or mixed-contract launch and return an actionable recovery path.
checks: The reported installed version/contract hash matches the actual absolute installed binary and assets.
An interrupted update cannot silently leave an old binary with new TUI/protocol files.
Schema incompatibility blocks unsafe rollback even when old executable files exist.

tasks.title: Implement artifact authentication, CI approvals and package metadata
steps: Separate candidate build/qualification from actual publishing and require the approved human/environment authorization before release side effects.
Use the accepted supported target matrix and verify actual runner/toolchain availability at execution time.
Produce the chosen signatures/provenance/checksum/SBOM or equivalent approved metadata without exposing credentials.
Pin or justify action/build dependencies and scope CI permissions/secret access minimally.
Make Homebrew or other selected distribution metadata point to exact tested immutable artifact hashes.
Fail publication preparation when any required artifact/platform/evidence identity is missing.
checks: Creating a candidate or test tag cannot accidentally bypass the final cutover approval.
Distribution metadata references the exact qualified artifact, not a mutable latest placeholder.
No signing/publication secret enters logs, source ZIPs or package content.

tasks.title: Validate the real built package in a clean disposable prefix
steps: Install the actual newly built package into a new prefix and invoke its absolute bwrk binary, not PATH fallback.
Verify runtime/binary/TUI/workflow/schema manifest identities and complete directory contents.
Initialize two projects and exercise planning, genuine claim/proof/review/finish, TUI, memory and operation readback.
Verify project isolation and shell-profile nonmutation.
Run upgrade/interruption/rollback-allowed/refusal cases against actual previous supported packages.
Record host/ABI/tar/permissions/runtime and package hashes for every case.
checks: The installed product exhibits the accepted new behavior without developer checkout dependencies.
A fake local release/controller cannot satisfy this test.
All prefix/project side effects are confined and rollback behavior is verified.

tasks.title: Validate real macOS and Linux target packages
steps: Execute build/install/service/TUI/upgrade smoke on each approved macOS/Linux architecture using actual native executors.
Cover BSD/GNU tar differences, executable/signing/ABI/runtime behavior, socket permissions and process cleanup.
Record supported terminal/runtime combinations and explicit unsupported environments.
Verify linked SQLite/features and complete package asset identity on the target, not only the build host.
Run at least the required genuine lifecycle/isolation/unknown-outcome paths using the installed absolute binary.
Treat missing platform access as blocked qualification rather than a fixture pass.
checks: Every supported target has actual native installed-package evidence.
No target is called supported on cross-compilation or fixture rendering alone.
Required platform failure blocks release until fixed or scope is explicitly changed before qualification.

tasks.title: Harden source archive generation and required-plan/source retention
steps: Retain the complete intended text source, installer .cjs files, required TUI tree, specs, migration code and implementation/evidence reports.
Verify manifest sizes/hashes, safe paths, required files and explicit exclusions from a clean source archive.
Ensure new production plan/evidence files are deliberately included or excluded by an explained source-package policy, not silently lost by suffix filtering.
Extract to an isolated checkout and run supported source-build/contract/TUI checks.
Preserve failed evidence and provenance without including secrets, raw credentials, node_modules or target outputs.
Keep source ZIP validation separate from rebuilt production binary/package qualification.
checks: A clean source ZIP contains every required source asset, including installer sources and full TUI tree.
Archive manifest validation is reproducible and catches missing/altered files.
Passing this task cannot by itself mark a production package or release ready.

tasks.title: Integrate distribution identity and upgrade evidence for qualification
steps: Reconcile source, build, package, installed-prefix and platform evidence into one immutable candidate identity graph.
Verify wizard/source/embedded bytes and binary/TUI/share contract versions agree.
Record approved upgrade/rollback/database compatibility and any remaining platform/security limitation.
Ensure future release qualification will rebuild/retest after later source changes instead of reusing these stale package passes.
Prepare exact publishing inputs and smoke commands without publishing or pushing tags in this task.
Provide independent distribution review with every failed and successful run.
checks: Every artifact and installed test maps to exact source/runtime identity.
There is no claim that a local package has already been published.
Later source changes visibly invalidate affected package evidence.

tasks.title: Write and execute fresh-user onboarding and parallel planning guide
steps: Document install, explicit project init, identity verification, milestone/tasks/cycle commitments and dependencies from an empty directory.
Use actual accepted command syntax and explain profiles, readiness, queued prerequisites and parallel agents.
Walk through genuine verification, optional configured review, finish/close and exact downstream progression.
Show the corresponding TUI navigation including short editor-terminal behavior.
Execute every command in a disposable installed-prefix project and capture corrected transcripts.
Avoid claims about deferred platforms/web/remote/automatic launching.
checks: A new reader can complete the supported workflow without chat history or internal source knowledge.
Every documented command exists and behaves as described.
The guide never equates complete/cancelled with accepted closed.

tasks.title: Document statuses, proof, independent review and explicit exceptions
steps: Explain primary status, secondary reasons, freshness and integrity using real product terminology and examples.
Distinguish queued/paused/retry/expired/failed proof/rejected review/operator hold/unavailable.
Explain pinned requirements, source/config applicability, failed-history retention and proof-complete closeout pending.
Document review independence and approve/reject/return/revoke consequences.
Explain reasoned revision-bound gate exceptions/edge waivers while preserving raw failure/unmet prerequisite truth.
Include safe next actions and links to actual inspection/recovery commands.
checks: A user can tell why progress is waiting and who can resolve it.
No internal enum/fence/SQL vocabulary is required for normal operation.
An exception is never described as evidence that a failed test passed.

tasks.title: Write incident, unknown-outcome and safe resource-recovery runbooks
steps: Document service unavailable/stale socket, unknown operation, expired attempt, still-running worker, disk failure and corrupted-record handling.
Start with read-only inspection and exact operation/project identity; prohibit blind retries, live-lock breaking and destructive resets.
Explain confirmed-stop/resource disposition before replacement and role-required recovery actions.
Provide escalation and evidence collection with redacted credentials and preserved failed artifacts.
Execute each supported recovery procedure in a disposable real-service failure scenario.
State residual platform/OS limits and unsupported repairs plainly.
checks: An operator can resolve tested incidents without direct SQLite edits or erasing history.
Unknown outcomes are resolved by original readback identity before retry.
Runbooks never advise force-breaking a verified live lock as normal recovery.

tasks.title: Write migration, backup/restore and source-memory maintenance guides
steps: Document supported legacy versions, complete disposition reports, ambiguous completion and required manual review.
Explain dry-run, original export preservation, explicit destination and no-silent-overwrite guarantees.
Document full database/blob/Git backup scope, restore epoch effects, compatibility and rollback limits.
Explain source parsing/citations/index lag, curated publication/reimport and recovery after Git/database partial completion.
Give safe retention/repair guidance preserving failed proof and historical provenance.
Verify examples against actual accepted migration/restore/memory evidence.
checks: Readers know which original data/behaviors are supported, retained-but-unaccepted or unsupported.
Backup instructions preserve more than the main SQLite file.
No doc implies restored live attempts can resume with old fences automatically.

tasks.title: Write install/update/rollback and support-platform documentation
steps: Publish actual supported OS/architecture/runtime/terminal requirements and tested artifact identities.
Document fresh install, explicit prefix, optional PATH changes, update/upgrade behavior and installed-version verification.
Explain active-service coordination, separate schema migration and safe rollback/refusal rules.
Distinguish source ZIP, local built candidate and published release artifacts.
Include offline/air-gapped installation only where explicitly supported and tested; do not imply offline mutations when the service is unavailable.
Execute instructions against disposable prefixes using the absolute installed binary.
checks: Install instructions obtain/verify the intended artifact rather than relying on stale PATH binaries.
Rollback guidance cannot corrupt a newer schema.
Supported-platform claims correspond to native evidence, not historical CI labels.

tasks.title: Publish support diagnostics, privacy and known-limitations policy
steps: Define a redacted diagnostic bundle with source/binary/schema/runtime IDs, relevant operations and logs without secrets or unrelated project data.
Document threat-model boundaries, credential handling, actor roles and responsible local incident response.
List only explicit approved noncritical deferrals/non-goals with owners and user-visible effects.
State that integrity/isolation/authority/proof blockers cannot be accepted by relabeling status or narrowing tests.
Define support escalation, evidence retention and release incident/rollback decision ownership.
Check the docs do not overclaim tamper-proof audit, remote safety or untested platform support.
checks: A support bundle can be shared without leaking credentials or other project contents.
Every advertised limitation is explicit and consistent with launch scope.
No must-have release blocker is hidden in a casual known-limitations note.

tasks.title: Run documentation and unfamiliar-user usability acceptance
steps: Have an independent reader execute onboarding, planning, completion, recovery and upgrade instructions against the installed candidate.
Validate all documented commands, examples, file paths, status terms and compatibility limits against current registries.
Check links/help/error messages and no-goal workflow references for stale internal names.
Test short-terminal navigation and recovery descriptions with actual UI behavior.
Record confusion and failed steps as findings, update artifacts through owners and rerun the corrected walkthrough.
Tie results to exact documentation/source/package identity.
checks: A new user completes the required path without bespoke coaching or source edits.
All examples are observed against the actual accepted product.
Documentation review is independent and retained findings are reconciled before release qualification.

tasks.title: Freeze the release candidate and complete evidence manifest
steps: Freeze a clean integrated source commit/tree and approved version/contract/schema identities with no untracked required files.
Resolve all must-have tasks/findings/required external inputs and identify exact supported target set.
Index current source, test, migration, no-goal, TUI, security, load and package evidence; reject stale or mismatched-source artifacts.
Record proposed release notes and permitted noncritical deferrals with explicit owner approval.

R-TUI-SMOKE.why: Mounted PTY service evidence and known gaps; fixture rendering is supplementary only.

decisions.title: Launch scope and vocabulary
decisions.recommendation: Retain D01-D29 local same-host macOS/Linux product boundaries; all core CLI/TUI/source/memory/no-goal work remains required.
decisions.required_resolution: Confirmation of final production scope, explicit non-goals and accepted terminology; no implicit scope expansion.

decisions.title: Project/entity/proof/fence identities
decisions.recommendation: Separate project snapshot, entity revision, proof revision, attempt fence, database restore epoch and service instance.
decisions.required_resolution: Versioned identity/revision contract and migration from conflated fields.

decisions.title: Authenticated principal and independence trust boundary
decisions.recommendation: Use authenticated principal/project membership, explicit roles/delegation and local OS limits; caller role strings are not authority.
decisions.required_resolution: Credential/bootstrap/revocation design and precise independent-review definition.

decisions.title: Cycle-backed sprint authority
decisions.recommendation: Adopt separate task decomposition and scheduling assignments, one canonical cycle with legacy sprint compatibility.
decisions.required_resolution: Explicit amendment to the bounded fixed-tree strategy, migration and rollback; no silent dual authority.

decisions.title: Sealed submissions and D22/D27 deadline policy
decisions.recommendation: Recommended: release safe execution ownership at immutable submission, keep human review separate; do not silently retain or change the two-hour completion policy.
decisions.required_resolution: Owner explicitly chooses budget/review coupling and approves any D22/D27 change with version/migration fixtures.

decisions.title: Status/actions/integrity/schedule version
decisions.recommendation: Retain queued for normal prerequisites; separate availability/integrity; approve exact precedence and server-owned actions.
decisions.required_resolution: Resolve scheduled/status-3 compatibility, primary reason tie/order and safe recovery actions.

decisions.title: Immutable requirements and relevant proof selection
decisions.recommendation: Separate pinned declarations, observations and decisions; filter by complete subject before recency.
decisions.required_resolution: Canonical gate vocabulary/stages, profile versions, source invalidation and summary/audit resolution.

decisions.title: Review outcomes and independence policy
decisions.recommendation: Required only when pinned profile demands it; typed reject/return/revoke distinct from missing proof.
decisions.required_resolution: Principal/delegation independence and effects on current/historical submissions.

decisions.title: Dependency/reopen/override impact
decisions.recommendation: Accepted-closed-only default; task edges and explicit typed exceptions with historical truth preservation.
decisions.required_resolution: Allowed endpoint kinds, upstream reopen consequences, cancellation disposition and prospective exception expiry.

decisions.title: Readback, jobs and protocol compatibility
decisions.recommendation: One transaction/action authority plus durable external jobs; timeout is unknown until authoritative readback.
decisions.required_resolution: Admission deadline and definitive-not-found rules; schema/API/status/workflow compatibility matrix.

decisions.title: Support/security/performance/release budgets
decisions.recommendation: Declare target matrix and budgets before measurement; authenticate artifacts and enforce actual linked-runtime policy.
decisions.required_resolution: Named native executors, fixed workload/environment thresholds, retention/backup/rollback and package trust policy.

decisions.title: Source/memory and retained legacy parity
decisions.recommendation: Project-local versioned sources, Git-published curated memory and complete retained-v1 disposition mapping.
decisions.required_resolution: Supported input kinds, citation/publication/retention policy and unresolved raw legacy evidence gates.

acceptance.negative_assertion: Unapproved semantic change blocks implementation.

acceptance.requirement: Fresh init and exact project/database binding
acceptance.negative_assertion: Copied/stale/foreign metadata must reject without leakage.
Lexically local but resolved-foreign targets must reject.
Forged actor/role or repeat init cannot enroll an operator.
New session cannot inherit stale fence or fake review independence.

acceptance.layer: Real requirements plus owned negative corruption
acceptance.negative_assertion: Deleting a result/definition instance never reduces required proof.
Wrong entity/proof/fence/epoch rejects independently.
Pause/dependency and expiry/hold preserve all reasons.
Due date does not extend/steal authority; at-deadline expiry applies.
Read eligibility is not a substitute for final transaction checks.
Timeout cannot create duplicate effects or a false definitive not-found.
No acknowledged success with missing required audit/outcome.
Competing claims yield one owner, including resource overlap.
Foreign/stale session cannot adopt live ownership implicitly.

acceptance.requirement: Heartbeat versus progress and hard budget
acceptance.negative_assertion: Renewal cannot extend hard budget or invalidate unrelated proof.
Expired work is not ready until safe disposition.
Database fence alone cannot authorize reuse while a process writes.
No blind redispatch or deleted failed attempts.
Caller-supplied digest cannot make wrong inputs current.

acceptance.requirement: Bounded verifier and authenticated cryptographic receipts
acceptance.negative_assertion: Fake receipt, wrong subject, timeout, output flood and altered bytes fail.
Unrelated newer history is inert; stale/failed current proof stays visible.

acceptance.requirement: Immutable submission and approved review/budget coupling
acceptance.negative_assertion: Submission is not close; ownership ends only under accepted safe policy.
Self/delegated self-review rejects; rejection does not become missing proof.
Passing proof without matching intent cannot auto-close.
A forced gate remains failed raw proof plus explicit exception.
Release never erases holds/operator-only policy.
Cancelled does not satisfy default prerequisites.
No old-proof reuse or silent rewriting of closed successors.
Expired waiver cannot authorize new work; old history remains explicit.
No duplicate writable sprint/cycle identity.
Carry-over commits both ends or neither and preserves task identity.
Reciprocal-edge race cannot commit a cycle; complete is not closed.
No fabricated container attempt or stale scope closure.
Loaded-page counts cannot masquerade as totals; deferrals are not successes.
Valid queued children are allowed; invalid requirements/graphs reject.
Valid siblings stay safe/useful; no invented replacement rows.
Old-project responses cannot repaint current project.
Failed parsing/old citations/foreign sources remain correctly classified.

acceptance.requirement: Draft versus Git-published memory and recovery
acceptance.negative_assertion: Commit-after-side-effect is read back, never fabricated or duplicated.

acceptance.requirement: Bounded cited handoff and no-goal guidance
acceptance.negative_assertion: No hidden chat context, untrusted argv or omitted critical obligations.

acceptance.requirement: Retention roots and no unsafe artifact collection
acceptance.negative_assertion: Required accepted/failed-history proof cannot be silently collected.
Done/complete prose cannot become accepted v2 closed.
A row-count pass cannot hide missing required artifacts.

acceptance.requirement: Full online backup/restore and exclusive maintenance
acceptance.negative_assertion: Coherent DB/blob/Git state; old epoch/fence cannot revive.
No unavailable route or alternate spelling bypass.

acceptance.requirement: Trusted workflow discovery and two-harness no-goal loop
acceptance.negative_assertion: Script-only/fake receipt results cannot close the gate.
No client lifecycle/SQLite authority or fixture normalization.
No resize wall or unreadable destructive default; cancel causes no mutation.
No hidden invariant loss, unbounded history scan or threshold manipulation.
No open critical advisory/trust issue or unauthenticated test backdoor.
Stale/missing/mixed assets and unsupported linked runtime reject.
No mixed install or unsafe database downgrade; read back actual version.
No aspirational commands, unsafe recovery or cross-project secret bundle.

acceptance.requirement: All strict gates and independent cutover
acceptance.negative_assertion: Missing/failed/unsupported required evidence blocks ship.

acceptance.requirement: Authorized immutable publication and future installs
acceptance.negative_assertion: Published bytes equal qualified bytes; no implicit external authorization.
